articles.body: LeBron James, the former Los Angeles Lakers’ icon, is a billionaire after playing for over two decades in the league. While he has been a force to be reckoned with inside the court in his debut season with the Philadelphia 76ers, LeBron James’ Beverly Hills property has been going through major transformations after articles.title: Draymond Green says Warriors have 'moved on' after Kristaps Porziņģis steps back from playing: 'You can't sit and worry about spoiled milk'
articles.summary: Porziņģis, who has not played a game this season while dealing with health issues, announced Friday that he will be stepping back from basketball indefinitel...
articles.body:
With Golden State center Kristaps Porziņģis unexpectedly taking a step away from basketball due to health issues , Warriors veteran Draymond Green says the team is not dwelling on his exit.

When speaking to The Athletic's Sam Amick on Thursday, Green said the Warriors have never had a "culture" of blame and bickering, and spoke about moving forward from Porziņģis regardless of how helpful he would've been on the court.

"No one's sitting around bashing this guy or even worried about him, for that matter. In our minds, we've moved forward with the players that we have here," Green told The Athletic. "We know what type of player he is. But I don't think anyone in here is sitting around waiting on him to walk through that door. Everybody's moved on in their mindset."

Green told The Athletic that Warriors general manager Mike Dunleavy told the team about the ongoing Porzingis situation ahead of the team's season opener against the Los Angeles Lakers. The situation was re-addressed last week, with Green saying the team told players that it was "moving forward."

Green repeated that the Warriors are focusing on the chances for others to step up, with the veteran mentioning journeyman center Charles Bassey and undrafted rookie Graham Ike as players with something to prove.

"Like I said, everybody's moved on. It's a next man up mentality, right?" Green told The Athletic. "You embrace those guys, and you pour into those guys, to try to help them with all that they can be helped with so that they could ultimately help this team. But you can't sit and worry about spoiled milk."

Porziņģis, who joined the Warriors after being traded in February, has yet to play for Golden State this season while dealing with a health issue . The 31-year-old Latvian center signed a two-year, $40 million contract this summer to return to the Warriors, but has reportedly not been paid that salary while he is away from the team.

Though neither Porziņģis or the Warriors have clarified what health problems the center has been dealing with, Porziņģis has a history with postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome (POTS) , a chronic condition that can affect the nervous system.

Without Porziņģis, Golden State is relying on Al Horford as a backup center behind Green, along with Bassey and Ike to fill out the depth.

articles.title: Hawks Hold Off Wizards, Box Score Stats, Highlights for Trae Young, CJ, Top Players with AD Out
articles.summary: Trae Young has yet to beat the Atlanta Hawks in two games against his former team.
articles.body:
Trae Young has yet to beat the Atlanta Hawks in two games against his former team.

Young and the Washington Wizards fell short of a comeback in a 139-132 NBA Cup group stage loss to the Atlanta Hawks on the road, just two days after losing to the Hawks at home.

Here's a look at the top performers from Friday's in-season tournament action, from which Wizards forward Anthony Davis was sidelined with a right ankle sprain.

The Wizards took an early lead thanks to a 22-8 run to close out Friday's first quarter.

It was the Hawks leading by seven points at the half, however, thanks in part to 16 points in 19 minutes from Nickeil Alexander-Walker.

Young was held in the first half to six points on 3-for-6 shooting from the field.

The Wizards were led by a combined 24 points from Kyshawn George and Tre Johnson, but trailed after committing 10 turnovers through two quarters.

The Hawks held onto their advantage in the third quarter as the Wizards struggled with rebounding and CJ McCollum, who is now coming off the bench for Atlanta, heated up down the stretch.

The Wizards, which trailed by 15 points with less than three minutes left on the clock, launched a late comeback push but were ultimately able to erase the deficit before the final buzzer.

The Wizards dropped to 4-5 (1-1 in NBA Cup play) with the loss, while the Hawks improved to 6-4 (1-0 in NBA Cup play).

Young will get his next chance to earn a first victory against his former team when the Hawks and Wizards match up again Jan. 11 in Washington, D.C.

articles.title: Purdue stunned by Valparaiso in double OT upset after buzzer-beating 3-pointer
articles.summary: Valpo hit last-second threes in overtime and double overtime to beat the Boilermakers on the road and secure one of the biggest upsets of the college basketb...
articles.body:
It might be November, but it already feels a bit like March. On Friday, Purdue was upset by Valparaiso on a 3-pointer that barely beat the buzzer.

The Beacons' 83-80 win came after the team forced overtime, and then double overtime. In double OT, with the game tied with four seconds left, junior guard Justus McNair took the ball down the court and hit a game-winning, buzzer-beating 3-pointer to beat the Boilermakers.

Instead of a cupcake matchup early in the regular season, Purdue found itself outscored 38-26 in the second half after a late surge from the Beacons, who were 19.5-point underdogs.

With a minute left, McNair scored a jumper that tied things up at 58-all. The Boilermakers were not able to get a game-winning score despite multiple chances, which sent the game to the first overtime.

Though Purdue took the lead again, Valpo kept the Boilermakers within two scores and eventually pulled back within three points.

Rakim Chaney was given a one-and-one from the free-throw line to get closer, but he missed his first shot. However, Chaney managed to get the rebound off his miss, and circled out for a 3-point attempt that rolled around the rim and in, beating the buzzer and forcing double OT.

In double OT, though, it was the Beacons who had the Boilermakers on their heels, taking the lead before the Boilermakers tied it up. A hook shot from junior Purdue center Daniel Jacobsen with four seconds left set up McNair for his game-winning moment, and an upset for Valparaiso, a university with an undergraduate enrollment just above 2,000 students.

Other than double overtime, Valpo did not lead at all during the game — and yet it still managed to pull off the win. The Beacons, who play in Division I's Missouri Valley Conference, are now 2-0 to start the 2026-27 season.

Purdue drops to 0-2. The Boilermakers opened the year with a matchup against No. 15 Gonzaga, but narrowly lost.

Though wildly unexpected, Valpo's victory is not the first major upset of the season, after Oklahoma was stunned by East Texas A&M at home on Monday. Considering the men's basketball season is only a week in, it spells well for more early madness going forward.

articles.title: NMSU, Northwestern State Women's CBB Players Each Score on Own Basket in Rare Mishaps
articles.summary: A pair of Division I women's college basketball games (Arkansas vs. Northwestern State and New Mexico State vs. Southern Utah) on Friday featured players scoring on their own baskets, per Ian Casselberry of Yahoo Sports.
articles.body:
A pair of Division I women's college basketball games (Arkansas vs. Northwestern State and New Mexico State vs. Southern Utah) on Friday featured players scoring on their own baskets, per Ian Casselberry of Yahoo Sports.

In the first instance , the Razorbacks trapped Northwestern State after the Demons inbounded the ball under their own basket. Lady Demons guard Karma Wynn ran to help out trapped teammate Chloe Donnell, who passed her the ball. However, Wynn then ran toward her own basket for a layup, giving Arkansas an early 18-12 lead en route to an 89-59 win.

The basket, of course, had no bearing on the result, and Wynn did have good moments otherwise, finishing with six points, four rebounds and two assists.

In the second scenario, Southern Utah was inbounding the ball up 61-60 with 20.9 seconds remaining in regulation.

New Mexico State guard Emma Christiano was in the right place at the right time and stole a Southern Utah in-bounds pass on the Aggies' side of the court. Unfortunately, Christiano then drove to her own basket and laid it in for two, giving Southern Utah a 63-60 lead.

However, NMSU prevailed anyway after forward Stacy Chovino made a layup, stole the ball and then hit another bucket (following a timeout) for a 64-63 lead. Southern Utah missed a jumper for the win, and the Aggies earned the victory.

articles.title: Angel Reese Supports Brother Julian at Pelicans vs. T-Wolves in Video After WNBA Finals Loss
articles.summary: Atlanta Dream forward Angel Reese was in attendance for the New Orleans Pelicans' home game against the Minnesota Timberwolves on Friday evening in support of her brother, Pels forward Julian Reese.
articles.body:
Atlanta Dream forward Angel Reese was in attendance for the New Orleans Pelicans' home game against the Minnesota Timberwolves on Friday evening in support of her brother, Pels forward Julian Reese.

Angel Reese just finished her third WNBA season and first with the Dream after two campaigns with the Chicago Sky. It was a great year for Reese and the Dream, who went to the WNBA Finals and pushed the Golden State Valkyries to seven games before losing the finale, 68-63.

Reese won the Defensive Player of the Year award and earned All-WNBA Second Team honors. She averaged 16.4 points, 12.1 rebounds, 2.8 assists and 1.8 steals per game.

Julian Reese didn't see any action on Friday, but he impressed when given the chance for the Washington Wizards during his rookie season last year, posting 11.8 points on 52.9 percent shooting, 10.5 rebounds and 1.4 steals per game.

articles.title: Purdue Stunned By Valparaiso in 2OT, Box Score Stats, Highlights & Reaction to Upset Loss
articles.summary: Purdue's bid to make it back into the AP Top 25 is off to a rocky start.
articles.body:
Purdue's bid to make it back into the AP Top 25 is off to a rocky start.

The Boilermakers fell to 0-2 for the first time since 1976 following a Friday night double-overtime upset to visiting Valparaiso.

The Boilermakers, which opened the season with a loss against No. 15 Gonzaga, reportedly paid $90,000 in order to play their second game of the campaign against Valpo.

Valparaiso true freshman Rakim Chaney put up a career-high 35 points while Purdue's Caden Pierce and Omer Mayer combined for just four. Here's a look at the top performers from Friday's upset.

Purdue claimed an early 19-4 lead over Valpo in a dominant first half during which the home team held the visitors to just two field goals in 20 minutes.

Things started to fall apart in the second half as Purdue's defense struggled to contain Valparaiso. The visitors chipped away at the lead before tying the score at 48 points with five and a half minutes left on the clock.

Cox missed an opportunity at a go-ahead three-pointer shortly before the game went to its first overtime.

Chaney stepped up by sending the game to double overtime with a clutch three-pointer.

Chaney fouled out in double overtime before Justus McNair hit his team's second buzzer-beater of the game to secure the upset victory.

Purdue was ranked 28th in the preseason AP Poll, breaking a streak of 79 straight weeks in the Top 25.

The Boilermakers will need to start turning things around quickly, starting with a Monday home game against Illinois State, in order to move back toward ranked status after the first 0-2 start of Matt Painter's coaching career.

articles.title: LeBron, Embiid Struggle as Cavs Rout 76ers, Box Score Stats, Highlights for Harden, Spida, More
articles.summary: The scorching-hot Philadelphia 76ers hit a roadblock in Cleveland on Friday evening as the Cavaliers caught fire early and put this game away well before the final buzzer en route to a 119-95 victory in this NBA Cup matchup.
articles.body:
The scorching-hot Philadelphia 76ers hit a roadblock in Cleveland on Friday evening as the Cavaliers caught fire early and put this game away well before the final buzzer en route to a 119-95 victory in this NBA Cup matchup.

The 76ers were 2.5-point favorites, per FanDuel Sportsbook , but the Cavs won easily thanks in part to a great defensive performance and a strong second unit that scored 44 points.

LeBron James' first game in Cleveland as a 76er didn't go well, as the 24-year veteran (11 as a Cavalier) shot just 3-of-12 en route to eight points and six turnovers. However, he did get a nice ovation from the crowd when introduced during the starting lineup announcements.

Philadelphia center Joel Embiid missed all nine of his field goal attempts, and the team as a whole made just 36 percent of its field goals (25 percent from three-point range).

Here's a look at some notable performances this evening.

Cleveland got out to a 33-22 lead after one quarter thanks in part to a 19-4 game-opening run. Donovan Mitchell scored the Cavs' first six buckets.

The Cavs' bench started showing its prowess early thanks to Maleek Thomas (12 points) and Thomas Bryant (13 points)

Mario Hezonja (15 points) led the Cavs' reserves in scoring.

Philadelphia stopped the bleeding in the second quarter and trailed by eight (62-54) at halftime. The 76ers even cut the lead to as low as two (67-65) in the third quarter after a James jumper with 7:54 remaining in the frame.

However, the Cavs were too strong and finished the quarter on a 24-9 run capped by Mitchell's stepback three:

Cleveland scored the first five points in the fourth quarter for a 29-9 run overall and never looked back.

The 8-2 76ers, who won five straight entering Friday, still hold the Eastern Conference's best record. They'll now visit the Chicago Bulls on Sunday before starting a three-game homestand.

The 5-4 Cavaliers will stay home to play the New York Knicks on Saturday before beginning a three-game Eastern Conference road trip.

articles.title: No. 4 UConn gets 83-71 win over No. 16 Michigan in national championship rematch
articles.summary: Braylon Mullins and Silas Demary Jr. combined for 44 points in the Huskies' decisive victory over the Wolverines at Boston's TD Garden.
articles.body:
Friday's meeting between No. 16 Michigan and No. 4 UConn was a rematch of last season's NCAA tournament national championship game , a 69-63 win for the Wolverines. However, two different teams took the floor at Boston's TD Garden, presumably a neutral-site game but with a very pro-Huskies crowd cheering UConn on to an 85-77 win .

Braylon Mullins led the Huskies with 23 points, knocking down three 3-pointers and hitting 10 of 11 free throws. Silas Demary Jr. followed with 21 points, 7 rebounds, 4 assists and 2 steals. Both players found some redemption after combining for 13 points in the national title game defeat .

Michigan featured an almost entirely new squad with Mike Boynton Jr. taking over as head coach after Dusty May left for the NBA's Dallas Mavericks . Stars Yaxel Lendeborg, Morez Johnson Jr. and Aday Mara moved on to the pros as well, all three among the top 12 selections in the 2026 NBA Draft .

Though UConn lost Alex Karaban and Tarris Reed Jr., while Solo Ball is out for the season after wrist surgery , the Huskies looked like the more assured team with players knowing their roles. By comparison, Michigan appeared to be in search of its identity with returning veterans attempting to lead while new pieces figure out how they fit together.

Both teams started quickly from the opening tip with new Wolverines center Moustapha Thiam dunking a lob from Eliot Cadeau, followed by Mullins drilling a 3-pointer for UConn.

The Huskies then ran out to an early lead with Mullins and Demary hitting shots from behind the arc, while Michigan's only source of offense was Cadeau. Demary stayed hot, scoring five points during a 10-6 surge that put UConn ahead by seven.

Michigan had an opportunity to close within one point when the UConn bench was called for a technical foul after objecting when the Wolverines' J.P. Estrella drew a foul on an offensive rebound. But Trey McKinney missed both of the technical foul free throws, and Estrella made only one of his two foul shots.

Knowing Michigan squandered a good chance, the Huskies fans got louder.

UConn closed the first half with an 11-2 run capped by a Colton Landrew pull-up 3-pointer that sent the Huskies into halftime with a 43-30 advantage. That lead built to 18 points five minutes into the second half.

McKinney helped Michigan chip away at the deficit with his 3-point shot. His third 3 of the game cut UConn's lead to 64-55 with 9:25 remaining.

However, the Huskies outscored the Wolverines 11-6 over the next four minutes to rebuild their advantage to 16 points. UConn's depth allowed head coach Dan Hurley to go at least three deep into the bench and get impactful minutes. Landrew finished with 14 points.

Meanwhile, Boynton was looking for answers from his reserves and couldn't find any for now. Michigan got only eight points from its bench.

McKinney scored 22 points for the Wolverines, shooting 4 for 9 from long range. Estrella added 19 points and 9 rebounds, shooting 6 of 7 from the floor and 7 for 8 on free throws. Roddy Gayle Jr. followed with 18 points and 3 steals.

UConn (2-0) next hosts Wagner on Monday. Michigan (1-1) is off until Wednesday, when Marquette visits Ann Arbor.

articles.title: LeBron's return to Cleveland highlights a new reality: Sixers' offense is a work in progress
articles.summary: LeBron James played his first game in Cleveland after choosing the 76ers this offseason. The result was a 119-105 loss.
articles.body:
CLEVELAND — About an hour before tipoff, 76ers forward LeBron James emerged from the visitors' tunnel, with a collection of fans gathered near the southeast corner of Rocket Arena cheering triumphantly. It was impossible to ignore what could have been.

It was like a scene from the Apple TV series "Dark Matter," where the protagonist finds himself in an alternate reality and ponders the possibility of playing it out. A world exists, somewhere in the basketball multiverse, where James decides to ride off into the sunset donning the Cavaliers' wine and gold — not the 76ers' red, white and blue.

On Friday night, aside from the very obvious fact that James indeed plays for Philadelphia now, everything else felt normal in Cleveland: the pregame warm-up, rife with greetings and on-court drills, the same ones he had done in this very building for years; the chalk toss in front of the Cavaliers' faithful. Even the in-arena announcer's energy when James was introduced last was met with raucous applause. And when he checked out with four minutes remaining, a standing ovation ensued.

But the most prominent theme from "Dark Matter" is that no matter how familiar a place looks and feels, it's not your reality. And James was reminded of that.

"Every game has its own challenges," James said following the Sixers' 119-95 loss . "I don't think [we were sharp] offensively as a group and I know I damn sure wasn't good at all. Look at the film and try to get better for Sunday."

It would be somewhat nit-picky to overly dissect the 76ers' performance Friday after an 8-2 start — especially considering how much doubt and uncertainty existed about multiple superstars co-existing. But something has to be said about an offense (which ranked 21st in efficiency before tip-off and will continue to drop after mustering only 95 points) that has yet to jell.

In its second meeting with Cleveland, Philly didn't operate overwhelmingly loose with the ball (with 15 total turnovers), but there was no purpose to its ball movement. Most of the Sixers' half-court actions were stagnant and head coach Nick Nurse's rotations — designed to stagger their superpowers — only led to less flow and control.

Joel Embiid, who finished with just six points on 0-for-9 shooting, continued his floor-spacing woes. He's now shooting an abysmal 3-for-28 from deep, which puts even more pressure on the likes of James, Tyrese Maxey and Jaylen Brown to keep defenses honest. The 76ers won't win many games where Embiid is that inefficient and dominates the ball like he did, with a whopping 41.7 usage rate in the opening 12 minutes.

"I believe in myself," Embiid said. "But when you're in these moments and nothing is going in, it's hard to not look at yourself and be down. But you have to keep going and working."

But isn't this why LeBron came here in the first place? It wasn't because the 76ers were necessarily seeking another offensive weapon — they were in desperate need of his offensive mind.

Coming into Friday night's game, James ranked in the 96th percentile in assist rate and his assist-to-usage ratio was at the highest of his career . Conventional logic says maybe give the guy who's among the league leaders in potential assists, rim assist rate and offensive RAPM the ball as much as possible (his current output is 10% lower than his career usage) — as well as keep Maxey on the floor as much as possible (Philly's already woeful offense falls off a cliff when he sits ).

Some of the 76ers' playmaking metrics are noisy, partially because the sample size is still small after only 10 games and partially because of their sheer star power. For instance, of lineups that have played at least 50 minutes together, the 76ers' starters are taking good shots (seventh in shot quality per PBP Stats). They're also eighth in passes made per game and seventh in secondary assists, which indicates a concerted effort to move the ball and generate good looks. This is more important than ranking 18th in assists and 21st in potential assists, both of which stem from shot-making luck.

Friday was an outlier in that James coughed the ball up six times, but his other offensive struggles — eight points on 12 shots — weren't that much different than what the 41-year-old has endured this season, with the lowest points per shot attempt of a long, successful career.

"Too many turnovers on my behalf," James said. "And I didn't put in a rhythm offensively all game. Couple of them were careless, couple of them were trying to make the right play and not being successful with it."

The 76ers have started the season on a high note and, thanks to an impressive, aggressive defense, have silenced a few naysayers in the opening weeks of the new campaign. But until their offense can find a happy medium, one that keeps James at the mental wheel and highlights the other stars in their respective roles — or if he can rediscover his scoring efficiency — their dreams of serious contention could be another alternate reality door.

articles.title: NBA Cup 2026: Luka Dončić's 53-point night leads Lakers comeback win, Cavaliers snap Sixers' 5-game winning streak
articles.summary: Luka Dončić couldn't be stopped in a Lakers comeback win.
articles.body:
Luka Dončić's MVP case got another boost in NBA Cup action on Friday.

The Los Angeles Lakers star dropped a season-high 53 points to key a 124-118 comeback win against the Portland Trail Blazers, who led by as many as 16 points in the first half but watched that advantage evaporate in an overwhelming third quarter.

Dončić foreshadowed that comeback at the end of the first half, when he banked in a shot from roughly three quarters down the court. It was measured at 61 feet in the NBA's play-by-play.

The performance was Dončić's sixth 40-point game of the season, an NBA best and four games better than the next-closest players. Dončić also became the first Laker since Kobe Bryant in 2012 to score 40 points in four straight games.

Dončić also has two of the three 50-point games in the NBA this season. He has scored at least 37 points in his last seven games.

Cavaliers enjoy a rough night for Joel Embiid and LeBron James

East Group B figures to be one of the most competitive groups in the 2026 NBA Cup. The Cleveland Cavaliers just gave themselves a major leg up on that leaderboard.

Cleveland began its NBA Cup opener with a 19-4 run against the Philadelphis 76ers, then effectively ended the game with a 12-0 run across the end of the third quarter and start of the fourth. The Cavs wound up winning 119-95 .

The loss snaps a five-game win streak for the Sixers, who are now 8-2 overall and 1-1 in Cup play. Their only other loss had been to the Detroit Pistons on the second leg of a back-to-back, while missing Joel Embiid and VJ Edgecombe.

The Cavaliers were without standout center Jarrett Allen due to a knee injury , a notable loss given the presence of Embiid on the other side. However, the former MVP big man had easily his worst game of the season, posting 6 points on 0-of-9 shooting with 7 rebounds, 2 blocks and 2 turnovers.

Combine that with LeBron James posting only 8 points on 3-of-12 shooting with 3 assists and 6 turnovers and it was a rough go for the Sixers, who were outscored 46-26 in the paint before James and the starters left the game for good.

Evan Mobley might have had something to do with that, as he finished with 22 points on 13 shots with 6 rebounds, 4 assists and his usual presence on defense. Donovan Mitchell had 23 points, 8 assists and 7 rebounds, leading the Cleveland offense all night.

It wasn't just Cavaliers players making shots either.

articles.title: Los Cavaliers bajan a los 76ers a la tierra en la visita de LeBron a Cleveland
articles.standfirst: LeBron James no tuvo su mejor noche con 8 puntos, 7 rebotes y 3 asistencias
articles.summary: LeBron James no tuvo su mejor noche con 8 puntos, 7 rebotes y 3 asistencias
articles.body: Los Cleveland Cavaliers derrotaron este viernes por 119-95 a los Philadelphia 76ers en la fase de grupos de la Copa de la NBA en el regreso de LeBron James a Cleveland, por primera vez desde que decidió fichar por el equipo los 76ers. El bahameño V.J. Edgecombe abrió el marcador con un mate para los 76ers, pero los Cavaliers respondieron con un parcial de 15-0 que cortó LeBron James tras casi cinco minutos en blanco. Nunca más se pusieron por delante los 76ers este viernes en Ohio, aunque estuvieron cerca en el tercer cuarto, después de ponerse a solo dos puntos (67-65) con otra canasta de LeBron. Un triple de James Harden inmediatamente después dio paso a un parcial de 52-30 hasta la bocina final favorable a los Cavaliers, que llegaron a disfrutar de una ventaja máxima de 25 puntos. Además de dejar tocados a los 76ers en la Copa de la NBA, donde una derrota puede salir muy cara, los Cavaliers terminaron con la racha de cinco victorias seguidas de Philadelphia, que solo había perdido ante los Detroit Pistons y que presenta un balance de 8-2. Donovan Mitchell completó el partido con 23 puntos, Evan Mobley con 22, James Harden con 17 y el croata Mario Hezonja firmó un doble-doble con 15 puntos y 10 rebotes. Para Philadelphia, Jaylen Brown terminó el partido con 20 puntos, Edgecombe con 19 puntos y Tyrese Maxey con 17. LeBron James no tuvo su mejor noche con 8 puntos, 7 rebotes y 3 asistencias. Los Cavaliers, el equipo en el que LeBron debutó en la NBA y con el que conquistó el anillo en 2016, aspiraban a recuperarlo este verano para su último baile. Sin embargo, el de Akron, ciudad situada a unos 45 minutos de Cleveland, se decantó por Filadelfia. Los Cavaliers (1-0) se sitúan al frente del Grupo B del Este de la Copa de la NBA tras su abultada victoria de este viernes. Los 76ers (1-1), por su parte, son terceros, también por detrás de los Miami Heat (1-0).

articles.title: NBA: LeBron James held to single-digit points for only 10th time as Philadelphia 76ers lose to Cleveland Cavaliers
articles.summary: LeBron James held to eight points as Philadelphia 76ers lose 119-95 on his return to Cleveland; the 41-year-old received smattering of boos from Cavaliers fans during first half; James spent 11 seasons over two stints with the Cavs
articles.body:
James was held to eight points as the Cavaliers routed the 76ers 119-95 in an NBA Cup group stage game.

The 41-year-old, a native of Akron, Ohio, who elected to sign with Philadelphia in the offseason, instead of returning to Cleveland for a third stint, was 3 of 12 from the field, including 0 for 4 on three-pointers, while he committed six turnovers in 31 minutes.

"Definitely not feeling a good rhythm offensively," James said. "We didn't look like much offensively. We had a couple spurts, but too many turnovers on my behalf."

James received a smattering of boos from Cavaliers fans every time he touched the ball during the first half.

And this time there was no video tribute to the four-time NBA champion - who won one of those titles with Cleveland in 2016. When visiting the Cavaliers last season, they showed highlights of him scoring 25-straight points during Game 5 of the 2007 Eastern Conference finals against the Detroit Pistons, which prompted him to tear up.

James spent 11 seasons over two stints with the Cavs. He left as a free agent in 2010 to join the Miami Heat, came back in 2014 and departed again in 2018 to join the Los Angeles Lakers.

"At the end of the day, nothing can get as worse as December 2, 2010, from a reception standpoint," James said. "I've seen them near the depths of hell when it comes to reception here all the way to the heavens above. So anything in between, it's easy money."

The 76ers' loss was James' second-worst in Cleveland as a visiting player. He is 9-5, but has been on the losing end in his last three trips. Philadelphia will return to Cleveland on March 1.

The Sixers came in with the NBA's best record but fell to 8-2. Head coach Nick Nurse was already looking ahead to Sunday's game at the Chicago Bulls.

"We were lacklustre and they were very, very good. And I think we expected them to be very good tonight considering that they had a couple tough losses in a row," Nurse said.

"We were not very good. Probably once in a while that's going to happen. Important thing is that we get over it and bounce back on Sunday."

articles.standfirst: Es el séptimo partido consecutivo que Doncic completa al menos 35 puntos, 5 rebotes y 5 asistencias, igualando un récord de Robertson; es el primer jugador de los Lakers desde Kobe Bryant en encadenar cuatro partidos seguidos con al menos 40 puntos

articles.body: Luka Doncic se exhibió este viernes con 53 puntos en el sufrido triunfo de los Lakers por 124-118 ante los Portland Trail Blazers, una victoria que mantiene a los angelinos con vida en la NBA Cup tras la derrota en su debut. La exhibición del esloveno incluyó una espectacular canasta desde tres cuartos de cancha sobre la bocina del descanso. Es el séptimo partido consecutivo que Doncic completa al menos 35 puntos, 5 rebotes y 5 asistencias, igualando un récord de Robertson. Además, se convirtió en el primer jugador de los Lakers desde Kobe Bryant en encadenar cuatro partidos seguidos con al menos 40 puntos. Los Lakers han empezado la temporada con un balance de 8 victorias y dos derrotas, aunque una de ellas fue en su debut en la NBA Cup, frente a los Golden State Warriors, un tropiezo que podría ser definitivo de cara a su pase a las eliminatorias. Tanto Warriors como San Antonio Spurs aún no han perdido en el Grupo C del Oeste en la competición, que comparten con Lakers, Blazers y Sacramento Kings. Los Blazers llegaron a tener 16 puntos de ventaja en el segundo cuarto, pero un parcial de 17-0 en le tercer cuarto, del 61-68 al 78-68 selló la remontada para los Lakers pese a la resistencia de Portland hasta el bocinazo final. Doncic cerró el partido con 53 puntos, 5 rebotes y 5 asistencias, con 20 puntos en ese tercer cuarto de la remontada angelina. Austin Reaves le acompañó con 25 puntos y Walker Kessler puso 16 puntos y 12 rebotes. Deni Avdija rozó el triple-doble para los Blazers con 22 puntos, 9 rebotes y 11 asistencias, Damian Lillard también aportó 22 puntos y Donovan Clingan completó otro doble-doble con 17 puntos y 11 rebotes. Es la segunda derrota de la temporada para unos Blazers que presentan un balance de 6-2.

articles.body: En Dallas, los Mavericks derrotaron a los Utah Jazz 112-100 en el debut del canario Santi Aldama con la franquicia texana, tras su traspaso este verano desde Memphis en plena recuperación de una operación en la rodilla. articles.summary: The Golden State Warriors are back in action on Saturday to continue their current six-game homestand, welcoming the Orlando Magic to the Chase Center.The Wa...
articles.body:
The Golden State Warriors are back in action on Saturday to continue their current six-game homestand, welcoming the Orlando Magic to the Chase Center.

The Warriors are on a six-game winning streak and are fresh off a 120-100 win over the Miami Heat.

On the other hand, the Magic have lost three in a row heading into Saturday's matchup. They started their four-game road trip with a 117-104 loss to the Phoenix Suns.

Golden State Warriors Injury Report vs. Magic

GettyJimmy Butler III #10 of the Golden State Warriors reacts during their game against the Houston Rockets in Game Four of the Western Conference First Round NBA Playoffs at Chase Center on April 28, 2025 in San Francisco, California.

According to the Golden State Warriors official injury report , three players are out and three players are questionable against the Orlando Magic.

Jimmy Butler , Moses Moody and Kristaps Porzingis remain sidelined as they deal with their respective injuries and illness.

Butler and Moody are on track to return later this season, while Porzingis' time with the Warriors could be coming to an end once a resolution to their issue is found.

Draymond Green , Gary Payton II and Gui Santos are all listed as questionable . They could get upgraded to available or downgraded to out before tip-off.

Green is dealing with right elbow soreness and inflammation, which is a new injury. Payton has right calf tightness and soreness, while Santos is still dealing with left knee tendinitis.

If Green can't play, Charles Bassey likely steps in and provides another spark for Golden State.

As for Payton and Santos, Will Richard played well in the Warriors' win against the Heat.

Kristaps Porzingis Provides Update on His Status

In a statement on his official X account , Kristaps Porzingis shared an update on his current status and issue with the Golden State Warriors.

"This season I was really looking forward to running it with this group, but as I ramped up, my body didn't respond the way I anticipated," Porziņgis wrote. "I'm doing good, but I know what it takes, and I'm not where I want to be to perform at the level that I expect from myself. At this point, I've made the decision to prioritize my health and step away from the game I love."

"In this situation, I want to show the utmost respect for the Golden State Warriors and work with them to find a solution that makes sense," he continued. "I'm thankful to my family and close ones for always being there. Much appreciation to all of you for the support. Onwards and upwards. "

Draymond Green reacted to Porzingis' statement and confirmed that the Warriors are moving on from him.

articles.title: Lakers rally past Blazers behind Dončić’s 53 points
articles.summary: Luka Dončić gave the Lakers a chance before halftime with a shot from beyond half court. In the third quarter, he helped turn that chance into control.
articles.body:
LOS ANGELES — Luka Dončić gave the Lakers a chance before halftime with a shot from beyond half court. In the third quarter, he helped turn that chance into control.

Dončić scored a season-high 53 points, including 20 in the third quarter, as the Lakers overcame a 16-point deficit to beat the Portland Trail Blazers 124-118 on Friday night at Crypto.com Arena.

The Lakers improved to 8-2 with their fourth straight win, avenging their Oct. 27 loss to Portland and earning their first NBA Cup win of the season.

It was Dončić's fourth 50-point regular-season game as a Laker and the 11th of his career.

He has scored 361 points through his first nine games this season, the most since Wilt Chamberlain scored 472 (insane!) through nine games in 1962-63, according to the Lakers.

Dončić is now at an average of 40.1 points per game which ranks third in NBA history through a player's first nine games of a season, behind only Chamberlain's starts in 1962-63 (52.4) and 1961-62 (50.6), according to the team.

"For now ... I don't have any words," coach JJ Redick said of Dončić's historic scoring surge.

Austin Reaves recovered from missing his first seven shots to finish with 25 points. Walker Kessler added 16 points and 12 rebounds, while Dončić contributed five rebounds and five assists.

The Lakers needed much of that production after an opening quarter in which they missed all 12 of their 3-point attempts. Portland made six of its 12 attempts from deep, building a 29-20 lead despite Dončić supplying half of L.A.'s points.

Redick had called an early timeout with Portland ahead 10-4 and the Lakers shooting 2 for 12 overall. The deficit eventually reached 16 in the second quarter, with Reaves unable to find his first basket until a runner ended his 0-for-7 start.

Still, Redick saw reasons to trust the offense.

The shots began to fall toward the end of the second quarter that ended in Dončić's longest bucket of the season.

Dončić banked in a heave from beyond half court at the buzzer (and I GOT IT!), cutting Portland's lead to 60-53. The Lakers entered halftime within seven despite shooting 4 for 23 from 3-point range.

"I thought it was an important shot to make. So that's why I decided to make it," Dončić said.

He carried that momentum into the third quarter.

The Lakers used a 20-8 run to move ahead 73-68, with Dončić scoring 11 points during that stretch. They went on to outscored Portland 34-15 in the period, taking an 87-75 lead into the fourth.

Portland made another push, but Dončić delivered a jumper in the lane with 28 seconds remaining to help protect the advantage.

L.A. also created extra opportunities through its defense and work on the offensive glass. The Lakers forced 24 turnovers and collected 17 offensive rebounds, overcoming an 11-for-37 night from beyond the arc.

Dončić acknowledged feeling tired afterward, but his assessment of how he was holding up remained simple.

He was asked about sustaining his production every night and he kept the focus on the result.

"As long as we win, I'm good with whatever I do."

articles.title: Knicks defend Taylor Swift after players name her 'fakest celebrity fan'
articles.summary: The pop superstar's appearances at NBA games were deemed "a little performative" by New York Knicks point guards Tyler Kolek and Miles McBride.
articles.body:
The New York Knicks has defended superstar Taylor Swift, after players named her as the fakest celebrity fan.

The basketball team's point guards Tyler Kolek and Miles McBride were asked who the least genuine celebrity Knicks fan was during a NBA 2K livestream on Thursday.

"At the Knicks games, I would say it's very performative, cause like they just want to be seen at the game, they're not necessarily fans. Maybe Taylor Swift?" Kolek responded.

In May and June this year, Swift attended Game Three of the NBA Eastern Conference Finals in Cleveland and Game Four of the NBA Finals in New York City .

"I don't know if I've seen her at any other games," Kolak said.

A spokesperson for the Knicks defended Swift on Friday, telling media: "Taylor Swift has been a Knicks fan for many years, has a long history with Madison Square Garden, and we are incredibly appreciative of her support of the organisation."

The BBC has approached the Knicks for comment.

McBride added that "everybody else is usually solid", citing actor Ben Stiller and comedian Tracy Morgan as examples.

Kolek joked he was "gonna get some hate from the Swifties" and noted "she's got a lot going on so she can't come all the time... it's a little performative".

During Game Four of the NBA Finals, Swift watched alongside musicians Este Haim, Alana Haim and actor Mariska Hargitay in matching blue shirts with either "Stevie Knicks", "Knickelback" or "Knickole Kidman" written in orange.

The Knicks later went on to win their first championship in over 50 years, beating the San Antonio Spurs 94-90 in Game Five - sending New York City into a frenzy.

Swift has attended other games in the past, including a game between the Chicago Bulls and the Knicks in October 2014 and a match up against Orlando Magic in November 2014.

The pop-star's connection with Madison Square Garden runs deep as she has performed there for two of her tours "Fearless" in 2009 and "Speak Now" in 2011.

In July this year, Swift and her husband Travis Kelce got married at Madison Square Garden , in a star-studded ceremony officiated by actor Adam Sandler.

Few details about the wedding have been released, with Swift's publicist confirming at the time both the singer and Kelce wore Christian Dior. Neither had bridesmaids or groomsmen.

Swift's brother, Austin Swift, served as her man of honour, and Jason Kelce, Travis's brother, was his best man.

articles.title: One Bold Trade Idea Solves Everything for New York Knicks
articles.summary: Winning an NBA championship in the apron era means facing impossibly difficult questions roughly 10 seconds after the celebratory parades end.
articles.body:
Winning an NBA championship in the apron era means facing impossibly difficult questions roughly 10 seconds after the celebratory parades end.

That's where the New York Knicks find themselves after their 2026 title: expensive, short on draft capital, inflexible and staring down the inevitability of attrition. Owner James Dolan professed immediate aversion to the second apron after the title. Mitchell Robinson was allowed to leave. Karl-Anthony Towns could be next after failing to reach an extension agreement in the offseason.

Slippage seems unavoidable...unless the Knicks act boldly to keep their title window ajar in the short term while freeing up the financial flexibility they need to prop it open for another couple of seasons.

To do that, New York must consider moving on from a critical piece of the core in Mikal Bridges.

Mikal Bridges is uniquely durable and provides playoff-tested two-way play for right around 20.0 percent of the salary cap, but moving him is the surest way to add the flexibility needed to retain more important pieces of the core—namely Karl-Anthony Towns.

If Bridges doesn't shake out of his brutal early-season slump, it'll be easy to argue that Strus and Derrick Jones Jr. actually improve the Knicks in the short term. The former has had no shortage of injury issues but is an even more proven playoff gunner than Bridges. The latter can defend wings at least as well as the current version of Bridges while providing decent three-point shooting and more athleticism in transition.

The real kicker is the savings. Strus and Jones Jr. are both on expiring contracts. If the Knicks want to retain one of them in free agency, they can do so at a much lower rate than Bridges' $36 million salary in 2027-28. If neither comes back, the Knicks will wipe out $108 million over the next three years.

Some of that cash could go to an extension for KAT, as New York is already giving some of Bridges' minutes to Landry Shamet, Jordan Clarkson and Duece McBride.

If you can get over the Villanova of it all, this deal might make the Knicks better right now while freeing them up to stay relevant in the contender conversation down the line.

This side of things is a little trickier. We should expect the Clippers to ask for New York's 2033 first-rounder as an incentive to take on Bridges' deal. Out five future picks as punishment for cap circumvention, LA needs all the first-round assets it can get.

Then again, the two seconds coming from New York could be part of a package that allows the Clips to move into the back of the first round in 2027. It's also not a given that Bridges' contract is underwater and needs a sweetener attached. His fit between Darius Garland and Brandon Ingram is ideal. His durability nicely offsets the frequent injuries that limit the other two.

While the Knicks might view Strus and Jones Jr.'s impending free agency as positives (because of the potential savings), the Clippers don't benefit similarly if those two walk away for nothing. Perhaps LA thinks it can get more for them in separate deals with other teams, but losing them in free agency would be a wasted opportunity.

Lastly, the Clips could always flip Bridges for a pick-centered package down the line if they don't view him as a valuable piece of their core. In a vacuum, he's still clearly the best asset in the trade. The Knicks are only shopping him out of necessity in this hypothetical.

articles.title: Luka Drops 53 as Lakers Beat Blazers, Full Box Score Stats, Highlights for Dame, Reaves, Top Players
articles.summary: Getting bored with only scoring 40 points on a nightly basis, Luka Dončić put up 53 on Friday night to lead the Los Angeles Lakers to a 124-118 victory over the Portland Trail Blazers.
articles.body:
Getting bored with only scoring 40 points on a nightly basis, Luka Dončić put up 53 on Friday night to lead the Los Angeles Lakers to a 124-118 victory over the Portland Trail Blazers.

Dončić's 53-point outing marks the highest single-game total for a player this season. It's also his fourth consecutive game with at least 40 points and sixth time overall hitting that mark in the Lakers' first 10 games.

Dončić is on one of the most incredible runs of his already-storied career. His four consecutive 40-point games makes him the first Lakers player to accomplish that feat since Kobe Bryant in January 2012.

The best evidence of how well things are going for Dončić came at the end of the first half when he sank a heave from roughly 60 feet away from the basket.

The six-time All-Star shot 17-of-33 from the field and made five threes against the Blazers. It's his seventh straight game with at least five three-pointers. He has raised his season-long scoring average to 40.1 points per contest.

Dončić received support from his teammates in the victory. Austin Reaves dropped a casual 25 points, giving him three straight games with at least 20.

Walker Kessler is reaping the benefits of playing with Dončić. The Lakers center finished with 16 points and 12 rebounds for his fourth double-double of the season, all of them coming since Oct. 28.

The Blazers put together a strong effort in defeat. The second quarter was a showdown between the two stars on both sides, as Damian Lillard outscored Dončić 12-10 in the frame en route to finishing with 22 points.

Since being held to a season-low nine points against the Memphis Grizzlies on Oct. 29, Lillard has rebounded with four straight 20-point outings. He's still trying to find consistency with his shot coming off the Achilles injury, though he did make four of his 10 three-point attempts against the Lakers.

Deni Avdija (22 points, 11 assists) and Donovan Clingan (17 points, 11 rebounds) both recorded double-doubles in the loss.

The difference in the game was the third quarter when the Lakers outscored Portland 34-15. They trailed by as many as 16 points in the first half, but got the lead up to 12 at the end of the third period.

Dončić and the Lakers are off on Saturday before kicking off a four-game road trip on Sunday with a marquee matchup against the Detroit Pistons.

Portland will play the second night of a back-to-back on Saturday when it hosts the San Antonio Spurs at the Moda Center.

articles.title: NBA Cup 2026 Standings, Bracket Predictions After November 6 Group Play
articles.summary: The Cleveland Cavaliers produced the most impressive win on the second Friday of play in the 2026 NBA Cup.
articles.body:
The Cleveland Cavaliers produced the most impressive win on the second Friday of play in the 2026 NBA Cup.

The Cavs handed the Philadelphia 76ers their second loss of the regular season, and in the process, opened up an edge in the point differential tiebreaker in East Group B.

Donovan Mitchell and Co. still have a few tough games left in East Group B, but Friday provided them with a nice start.

Over in the Western Conference, Luka Doncic's 53-point game against the Portland Trail Blazers allowed the Los Angeles Lakers to remain in contention for the Group C crown.

The Lakers need to be perfect and get a bit of help during the rest of the group stage to win Group C.

West Group B also has the potential to be fun until the final group-stage minute because of how well the Minnesota Timberwolves and Oklahoma City Thunder are playing. Both teams picked up victories on Friday night.

Cleveland picked up Friday's biggest win in the Eastern Conference.

The Cavs beat the 76ers by 24 points to take over the lead in East Group B and put the Sixers in a tough spot with their point differential.

Cleveland's only game into its NBA Cup schedule, so plenty can change in Group B, but Friday provided a good launching point for Donovan Mitchell and Co. in the competition.

All five teams in Group B have a chance to win the group, but Cleveland and Miami are the only ones that can take first place by winning out and receiving no help.

The Sixers need to beat the Heat and Pacers by decent-sized margins to make up for the severity of Friday's loss.

You could argue the Knicks are in the best shape because they play the Cavs and Heat at home to finish out group play at the end of the month.

Boston is the clear front-runner in Group C with its 2-0 record and massive positive point differential.

Group A seems like it is down to Orlando, Toronto and Detroit. The Raptors pulled themselves back into contention with a double-digit win over the Bucks, but they're in a tough spot because their NBA Cup loss is to the Magic.

Detroit is playing the best early basketball of the three Group A contenders, and that's all without Jalen Duren on the floor.

Luka Doncic and the Los Angeles Lakers rebounded from last week's loss to Golden State with a win over Damian Lillard and Portland on Friday.

Doncic's 53-point performance pulled the Lakers back into contention in a tough group headlined by Golden State and San Antonio.

The Lakers must beat the Spurs to have any chance of getting into the knockout round, either as the Group C winner or the best second-place team.

Victor Wembanyama and the Spurs get Steph Curry and the Warriors at home next Friday in a game that will determine the Group C front-runner. The Spurs hold the edge because of the home court.

Oklahoma City could benefit from playing Minnesota at home in what is now Group B's biggest game.

The Thunder are only one point back on point differential of the Wolves with an extra game in hand. It feels like Group B is theirs to lose.

Denver likely has the edge in Group A for a similar reason as OKC in Group B. The Nuggets get Dallas at home in what will likely be the game that decides Group A.

Minnesota's point differential looks great right now. The early buildup of high-margin wins could allow the Wolves to advance as the best second-place team if they keep it competitive with OKC.

articles.summary: Stephen Curry, the Golden State Warriors’ star player, and his wife, Ayesha Curry, have been able to build a profitable investment portfolio in the last
articles.body: Stephen Curry, the Golden State Warriors’ star player, and his wife, Ayesha Curry, have been able to build a profitable investment portfolio in the last decade. While the two continue to work on their ventures together, Stephen Curry and his wife, Ayesha Curry, have also been pretty strategic when it comes to investing in real estate.Stephen Curry had to sell a property at a loss in one of the costliest neighborhoods in the countryA few years ago, in 2019, the four time NBA champion Stephen Curry paid a whopping $31 million for a luxurious 17,000+ square feet mansion in Atherton, California.The luxurious property was located at Atherton's exclusive Redwood Oaks neighbourhood which has consistently ranked among the wealthiest ZIP codes in the United States.The sprawling property has seven bedrooms, nine bathrooms and a two story atrium. Along with that, it also has a indoor-outdoor living room, an expansive wine cellar, a private movie theatre, and a fully equipped bar.The 17,000 square feet property also consists of a resort style swimming pool and cabana with a fireplace, formal gardens, extensive manicured lawns, a standalone guest house, and a private walnut orchard.While Stephen Curry, his wife, Ayesha Curry, and their four children lived in the luxurious estate for quite a while, the property faced a lot of issues when it came to being sold.Earlier this year, Stephen Curry listed his Atherton property for sale for $36 million. Despite the luxurious zip code, it seems the property failed to make a mark among buyers and was ultimately sold at a loss.A few months ago, as per reports, the four time NBA champion Stephen Curry was ultimately able to sell the property for $900,000, incurring a loss of $100,000.It is not confirmed why the Golden State Warriors’ star Stephen Curry and his wife, Ayesha Curry, decided to sell their palatial property at a loss.Stephen Curry and Ayesha Curry’s security faced concerns at their Atherton residenceInterestingly, Stephen Curry’s former Atherton mansion had also found itself in the middle of many legal controversies.In December 2023, Stephen Curry and Ayesha Curry’s security was compromised when an intruder breached the estate's security gate and entered the family's living room before being confronted by the nanny and subsequently arrestedHowever, the four time NBA champion Stephen Curry and his wife, Ayesha Curry, remained private about the incident as they focused on protecting their children.While the Golden State Warriors’ star player Stephen Curry ended up selling the Atherton residence, he and his family continue to own a $50 million coastal estate in Malibu, an $8 million luxury condo at the Four Seasons in San Francisco, a vacation home in Winter Park, Florida, and a commercial site in SF's Dogpatch district.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 2026 Arizona Fall Stars Game Features Four Orioles Prospects
articles.summary: The Baltimore Orioles will have four prospects representing the organization during Sunday's Fall Stars Game in Scottsdale, Arizona. With the Orioles rebuild...
articles.body:
The Baltimore Orioles will have four prospects representing the organization during Sunday's Fall Stars Game in Scottsdale, Arizona. With the Orioles rebuilding their farm system after several former first-round picks have graduated to the Major Leagues, it's a great time to see how well the remaining pieces are coming along. It also provides insight into where the team's future lies before the likely MLB lockout in December.

The team will have two pitchers on the roster, along with two outfielders who have been playing in the Arizona Fall League . These four prospects could also take the opportunity to shine for the organization, either as a potential player going forward or as a trade chip whenever the CBA negotiations are over.

Bragg, the No. 22 prospect in the Orioles' farm system, was a rising player in 2025 after posting a 1.24 ERA in the first half of the year and 67 strikeouts. He finished the year with a 1.68 ERA and 77 strikeouts over 59 innings, while only walking 17 and surrendering three home runs. He still holds a strong four-pitch arsenal, along with a 60-grade control.

The former eighth-round pick did not pitch in 2026, however, after undergoing Tommy John surgery at the end of the 2025 season. It knocked out what could have been his debut season at Triple-A if he had kept up his strong performance at Double-A. At 26, he still has time to adjust to his new post-injury mechanics, but he's running out of time to be as effective as he once was.

Bragg returned to baseball in the Fall League this year with Peoria, throwing a 3.60 ERA along with nine strikeouts in 15 innings and only three walks. There are questions about his velocity and his control, but his basics are still there. Per MLB , his heater did touch 95.6 miles per hour, and his high-70s sweeper still has enough movement to be effective at the Major level. His return to the mound in the Fall Stars Game, and continued march towards a spot on the roster, will be closely watched in this game and beyond.

Like Bragg, Reilly suffered a torn UCL injury in 2025 that ended his season prematurely and forced him to undergo Tommy John Surgery. Unlike his counterpart, the Fall Stars Game won't be the second time he's appeared in action this year. Reilly does not grade out anywhere on Pipeline's top-30 roster for the Orioles, which doesn't really sit right given that he earned high marks for his eight starts at the Double-A level. He did have a 3.63 ERA and 41 hits surrendered over 39 2/3 innings, but he holds 55 strikeouts over that same period.

Even in the Fall League, alongside Bragg, he generated a whiff rate of 40% or more on his slider, cutter, and curveball. He did need some work on his Fastball, which only has a 17% chase rate, but overall, his strikeout rate sat in the 95th percentile. If he succeeds in Sunday's game, there could be some chatter around him being moved during the offseason when trading resumes.

Honeycutt was one of the high-ranking prospects in 2025 for the team , placing fifth, before falling off the list altogether. That's mainly due to his catastrophically high strikeout rate of more than 40% and a low walk rate to coincide with it. The former 2024 first-rounder is likely on his last chance with the organization to piece all his tools together.

There were some signs of growth in Honeycutt's performance, finally eclipsing the .700 OPS mark for the first time since being drafted. He also did swipe a career-high 38 bases, and 15 home runs despite striking out 131 times in 293 at-bats. The strikeouts are a major problem for him and continue to hold him back, dropping his hit grade to 40.

The good news is that Honeycutt shone at Peoria in the fall league, holding a .275/.500/.575 slash line along with three home runs and five stolen bases. Shockingly, he had more walks than strikeouts for the first time in his entire baseball career. Perhaps there might be life in his career after all, though he still has a lot of work to do.

Easily their highest-ranking player for the team in the Fall Stars Game, Irish ranks 95th in the MLB Pipeline's top-100 prospects chart . Despite not exactly excelling in a singular area, he is well put together to have a successful career in the outfield. He could serve as either a backup behind the wave of other prospects or be a critical trade piece for desperate teams.

Irish had a breakout season in 2026 , holding a .916 OPS that saw a slugging average above .500 and swiping 20 bases in 76 games. He is in line to have a starting job alongside Colton Cowser and Dylan Beavers within the next year or two. Keep in mind that he still needs to perform at the Double-A and Triple-A levels before he gets a serious look. Irish made his case in Peoria with a .305 average and four stolen bases over 16 games. Like Honeycutt, he will likely see an at-bat or two in Scottsdale on Sunday, and some fielding action. Unlike Honeycutt, Irish is in a good position for a promotion to Double-A in 2027.

All four of the Orioles' representatives to Scottsdale for the Fall Stars Game have their own unique story and a path to the Major Leagues in due time. Even though this is one game out of the Fall Baseball League, it shows the four players have made tremendous progress to be showcased in a pivotal game.

articles.title: LeBron James Talks Reception From Cavs Fans in Video, Says He's Seen 'The Depths of Hell'
articles.summary: In the aftermath of the Philadelphia 76ers' 119-95 loss to the Cleveland Cavaliers on Friday night, LeBron James addressed the warm reception he received from the fans at Rocket Arena.
articles.body:
In the aftermath of the Philadelphia 76ers' 119-95 loss to the Cleveland Cavaliers on Friday night, LeBron James addressed the warm reception he received from the fans at Rocket Arena.

Asked if he was surprised by the cheers that greeted him during pregame introductions, James told reporters he has experienced "the depths of hell" to "the heavens above" from Cavs fans in his career (starts at 1:20 mark).

James was greeted with a series of applause from Cleveland fans when his name was announced prior to tipoff.

It didn't seem likely that James would receive any boos, but after he opted to sign with the 76ers over the summer from a group of finalists that included Cleveland, perhaps there was a chance he could hear some jeers.

The "depths of hell" James referenced is from his initial return to Cleveland as a member of the Miami Heat on Dec. 2, 2010.

Rob Brown, a security guard for the Heat, told ESPN's Dave McMenamin and Brian Windhorst in 2018 at one point during James' return game a member of NBA security wanted to end the game early because objects were constantly being thrown by fans.

"I remember a member of the NBA's security team wanted to call the game because there was so much coming at us during the game and we were basically ducking behind the scorer's table just to not get hit," Brown said.

Any of that bad blood from Cavs fans toward James evaporated forever when he returned to the team as a free agent in 2014, then led them to an NBA championship during the 2015-16 season.

Even after James left Cleveland to sign with the Los Angeles Lakers in the summer of 2018, Cavs fans gave him a huge ovation in his first game back during the 2018-19 season.

Cavs fans had plenty to cheer about after the pregame introductions on Friday. They held Philadelphia to 95 points in arguably their best all-around performance thus far.

James finished with a season-low eight points and had twice as many turnovers (six) as assists (three).

Golden State Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg started out his NBA career by buying his mother a house.

Lendeborg shared a video Friday on his YouTube channel in which he presented his mother, Yissel Raposo, with keys to a new home in California.

Lendeborg wrote a tribute to his mother last February in the Players' Tribune in which he detailed her ongoing battle with Stage 4 appendix cancer .

Raposo was later present to celebrate with Lendeborg when he was selected by the Warriors with the No. 11 pick of the 2026 draft.

Lendeborg has opened his rookie season by starting all nine games for the 6-3 Warriors while ranking behind only Stephen Curry for the team scoring lead with 21 points per contest.

articles.title: Lakers' Luka Doncic Talks Potential Pursuit of Wilt Chamberlain Record Amid Historic Start to Season
articles.summary: Los Angles Lakers star Luka Dončić says there's a "long season" standing between him and the possibility of joining Wilt Chamberlain as the second NBA player to average 40 points per game.
articles.body:
Los Angles Lakers star Luka Dončić says there's a "long season" standing between him and the possibility of joining Wilt Chamberlain as the second NBA player to average 40 points per game.

"It's obviously a long season. We're just 10 games in. We've got 72 left," Dončić told reporters when asked about chasing Chamberlain's record after putting up 53 points in a Friday night win over the Portland Trail Blazers.

"As long as we'll win, I'm good. Obviously, got 'em up today, not going to lie. Hopefully it continues, but you never know."

Dončić has averaged 40.1 points per game so far this season, joining Chamberlain as the only players to remain over the 40-point plateau nine games into an NBA campaign.

Dončić won the NBA scoring race for the second time in his career with 33.5 points per game last season with the Lakers. He set a career high by posting 33.9 points per game when playing for the Dallas Mavericks in 2023-24.

He has so far averaged more points per minute than Chamberlain recorded when posting 50.4 points per game in his 1961-62 campaign.

Dončić will need to keep up the efficiency that has seen him shooting 49.8 percent from the field and 41.9 percent from deep in order to keep up that pace down the stretch.

He and the Lakers, which are off to a Western Conference-best 8-2 start to the season, are set to return to action Sunday evening at the Detroit Pistons.

articles.title: LeBron James Jokes About Rethinking Golf Hobby After Dropping New Video of Round in Oregon
articles.summary: Philadelphia 76ers star LeBron James is questioning his love for golf after a difficult round at Pumpkin Ridge Golf Club outside Portland, Oregon.
articles.body:
Philadelphia 76ers star LeBron James is questioning his love for golf after a difficult round at Pumpkin Ridge Golf Club outside Portland, Oregon.

James joked his experience at Pumpkin Ridge "had me rethinking my love for the game" in a comment on his own video shared Saturday on his YouTube channel.

"Whose f--king bright idea was it to start a golf YouTube channel? I don't know who it was," James said in a narration at the beginning of the video. "I don't know whose stupid idea it was to do this. Add more stress to your f--king life when you're almost at the end of your basketball career to lessen the stress in your life."

James debuted his new YouTube channel by sharing a look at a golf trip with his former Cleveland Cavaliers teammates in Scotland.

He was recently in the Portland area as part of what he described as his annual trip to Nike headquarters.

The NBA's all-time leading scorer is eight games into his first season in Philadelphia. James has averaged 14.8 points, 7.4 rebounds, 6.9 assists and 1.5 steals per game to help the 76ers lead the conference with an 8-2 start to the campaign.

articles.title: El partido que desafía al paso del tiempo: aquí el DNI puede esperar
articles.standfirst: La Laguna Tenerife y Asisa Joventut juegan este domingo (13.00 h.p.) un encuentro que reúne a 17 jugadores de 30 o más años. Será a puerta cerrada por la borrasca Bruna
articles.summary: La Laguna Tenerife y Asisa Joventut juegan este domingo (13.00 h.p.) un encuentro que reúne a 17 jugadores de 30 o más años. Será a puerta cerrada por la borrasca Bruna
articles.body: Hay partidos que se juegan contra un rival. Y otros, contra el paso del tiempo. El La Laguna Tenerife-Asisa Joventut de este domingo (13.00 horas), que se jugará a puerta cerrada por la llegada de la borrasca Bruna, pertenece a esta segunda categoría. Sobre el parquet del Santiago Martín se reunirán hasta 17 jugadores de 30 o más años, nueve de ellos con 35 o más. Una colección de talento, experiencia y longevidad que convierte el encuentro en el partido más veterano del torneo. Un duelo sin fecha de caducidad en el que el DNI importa bastante menos que lo que sucede con un balón entre las manos. Txus Vidorreta, actual entrenador del Unicaja, dejó una frase para la reflexión cuando dirigía al conjunto aurinegro. Cansado de que le preguntaran por la edad de su plantilla, decidió cambiar el foco de la conversación y poner el acento en el talento: “Teniendo en cuenta que se habla mucho de la edad de mis jugadores, yo hablo de lo buenos que son. Mientras estén a tope no vamos a mirar el DNI”, dijo en una entrevista con Gigantes del Basket. Sus palabras adquieren un significado especial en una cita que reunirá a los tres jugadores más veteranos de la ACB: Marcelinho Huertas (43 años), Aaron Doornekamp (40) y Ante Tomic (39). Los dos primeros defienden los colores del Tenerife, un equipo que ha convertido la experiencia en una de sus señas de identidad. A su lado aparecen Gio Shermadini (37), Tim Abromaitis (37), Bruno Fitipaldo (35), Jaime Fernández (33), Vince Hunter (32), Ethan Happ (30) y Wesley Van Beck (30). En semejante contexto, Kyle Guy y López-Aróstegui, ambos con 29 años, casi parecen los júniors del equipo. Jaka Lakovic conoce perfectamente el valor de la veteranía. El actual técnico tinerfeño prolongó su carrera como jugador hasta los 38 años en el Barça B y compartió cancha con muchos de los protagonistas que se encontrarán este domingo. Por eso, su análisis va mucho más allá de las estadísticas o de la capacidad para resistir físicamente: "Los líderes que llevan mucho tiempo en el club han vivido muchas situaciones y siguen teniendo hambre de victoria. No sólo importa lo que hacen en la pista, sino su capacidad para gestionar emocionalmente al equipo y transmitir experiencia". Si alguien puede presumir de desafiar al calendario es Marcelinho Huertas. A sus 43 años, el brasileño continúa dirigiendo el juego con la clarividencia de siempre y contempla con naturalidad, incluso con humor, la veteranía de su equipo. "Por supuesto que bromeamos con el tema de la edad, somos un equipo con mucho sentido del humor. Somos el equipo más viejo del mundo. Es muy bonito tener un grupo con la misma mentalidad, con cosas en común y el día a día es mucho mejor. El ambiente es fantástico, llevamos mucho tiempo juntos. Es una gran y vieja familia, tenemos muchas cosas en común y sabemos de baloncesto", explicó en Eurohoops el pasado curso antes de la Final Four de la BCL. El base brasileño no esconde que la edad puede pasar factura en determinados aspectos del juego. La potencia y la velocidad pueden ser menores a las de hace una década, pero hay otros recursos que compensan una posible desventaja física: la lectura del juego, la inteligencia y la capacidad para interpretar cada situación. "Este es un grupo que posee mucha experiencia y compuesto por jugadores muy inteligentes y que saben entender la filosofía y todo lo que pide el entrenador. El único inconveniente que podría haber es el tema físico, y el competir contra equipos que son mucho más jóvenes", reconoció en SuperBasket Canarias. Al otro lado de la cancha habrá un rival que tampoco necesita mirar demasiado su documento de identidad para reivindicar su experiencia. El Asisa Joventut presenta una nómina de veteranos capaz de competir con la del conjunto insular. Ante Tomic (39) encabeza el grupo, acompañado por Ricky Rubio (36), Nico Laprovittola (36), Álex Reyes (32), Nikola Radicevic (32), Kwan Cheatham (31), Emir Sulejmanovic (31) y Lude Hakanson (30). Simon Birgander (29) completa una plantilla en la que la experiencia convive con el talento de los más jóvenes. Dani Miret, técnico verdinegro, entiende esa combinación como una de las grandes fortalezas de su equipo. La veteranía aporta conocimiento y oficio, pero necesita complementarse con energía y juventud para construir un proyecto competitivo. "Tenemos varios jugadores veteranos que han conseguido muchos éxitos, y esto nos tiene que ayudar. Pero creemos que todo es compatible, que para triunfar hacen falta jóvenes para que cuando seamos capaces de sacarles el máximo rendimiento sepamos rodearlos bien, y con esa mezcla de veteranía y juventud hagamos un equipo que por su singularidad sea peligroso". Pocos jugadores representan mejor esa mezcla de juventud y experiencia que Ricky Rubio. A sus 36 años, el base catalán acumula una trayectoria extraordinaria desde que debutó en la Liga ACB con apenas 14 años, 11 meses y 24 días, estableciendo un récord de precocidad. Ha vivido prácticamente todas las etapas posibles del baloncesto profesional y ahora contempla la veteranía desde una perspectiva diferente. "La edad es solo un número. Tenemos veteranos que saben jugar. Eso ayuda muchísimo a que todo el equipo esté conectado. Queremos ese Joventut ilusionante, ahora un poco veterano, pero que sigan viniendo jóvenes por detrás, esa es la marca del club", explicó en DAZN. En su equipo, Ante Tomic representa otra forma de entender el paso de los años. El pívot croata reconoce que buena parte de lo que sabe se lo enseñaron jugadores experimentados con los que compartió vestuario en los inicios de su carrera. "En mis primeros pasos en Zagreb y en el Real Madrid aprendí más de los veteranos que de todos los entrenadores que tuve. Lo más bonito de ser veterano es transmitir esa experiencia y creo que en estos años en el Joventut los jóvenes han podido aprender mucho de mí", dijo en Gigantes del Basket. Tomic no se limita a ejercer de referente por su trayectoria. También está dispuesto a compartir sus conocimientos con quienes vienen por detrás, sin necesidad de grandes discursos ni lecciones magistrales. "Los jóvenes saben que me pueden preguntar y que tienen mi apoyo, y eso es más que suficiente". Y deja a menudo una reflexión que explica buena parte de su longevidad deportiva: "La experiencia sí que me ha hecho mejor. Estoy más centrado en lo que puedo hacer o no". Este domingo, La Laguna Tenerife y Asisa Joventut pondrán frente a frente dos plantillas que han encontrado en la veteranía una virtud, no un inconveniente. Huertas, Doornekamp, Tomic, Ricky o Shermadini desafiarán una vez más al calendario en un partido en el que la experiencia cotiza al alza. Porque, como defendía Vidorreta, mientras el talento siga intacto, el DNI puede esperar.
