articles.title: In 2024, NBA star Trae Young helped open an Oklahoma Youth Sports Center with a $4 million gift; 2 years later, he pledged $100,000 to help Washington families
articles.summary: In Feb. 2024, Trae Young helped bring a major sports facility to Norman, Oklahoma, with a $4 million contribution from his family foundation.
articles.body: In Feb. 2024, Trae Young helped bring a major sports facility to Norman, Oklahoma, with a $4 million contribution from his family foundation. The Young Family Athletic Center opened with basketball and volleyball courts, swimming pools and sports programmes for local families. Two years later, the NBA guard made another community commitment, this time in Washington, D.C. Young and the Trae Young Family Foundation pledged $100,000 to two organisations supporting college education and food access. The Washington Wizards guard received the NBA Cares Bob Lanier Community Assist Award in October 2026 for his work in both communities. It was his third time receiving the honour.Trae Young's $4 million contribution helped bring a sports center to NormanYoung grew up in Norman, Oklahoma, and wanted to support the community where he spent his childhood. His family had to travel to give him access to different sporting opportunities when he was younger. The athletic center was planned to make more facilities available to children and families in the area.The project was part of Norman Forward, a community development initiative backed by local voters. The Young Family Foundation contributed $4 million towards its development. According to the City of Norman, it was the largest donation in the city's history at the time.The overall project cost was approximately $42 million, meaning Young's contribution was part of a much larger funding effort.The Young Family Athletic Center officially opened on February 19, 2024. Located on a 12-acre site in north Norman, the facility covers approximately 122,000 square feet.It was designed to accommodate several sports rather than focus only on basketball. The main gymnasium has eight basketball courts that can be converted into 12 volleyball courts. The aquatic section includes an eight-lane, 25-yard competition pool and a four-lane recreational pool.The facility also has a sports medicine and human performance section through its partnership with Norman Regional Health System.The Oklahoma facility offers basketball, volleyball and swimming opportunitiesThe Norman center provides facilities for both organised sports and recreational activities. Children can take part in basketball and volleyball programmes, while swimmers have access to the competition and recreational pools.The building also hosts youth leagues, sports camps and tournaments throughout the year. Families can access the facility through memberships and day passes.Its range of activities means children do not have to be interested in basketball to benefit from the project. The centre provides space for several sports and allows local organisations to host competitions and training sessions.The partnership with Norman Regional Health System also brings sports medicine and performance services into the facility. This gives athletes access to services beyond the courts and swimming pools.Young's contribution helped make the project possible, but the center was a wider community effort involving public funding and other partners. The city developed the project through Norman Forward, while the Young Family Foundation provided its $4 million gift.The opening in 2024 was an important step in Young's efforts to support youth recreation in his hometown.Trae Young planned a second athletic center in Oklahoma in 2026Young's foundation continued its work in Oklahoma after the Norman facility opened. In July 2026, Young and his foundation announced plans for a second youth sports and recreation center in Yukon. The proposed facility will follow the Norman model, with convertible basketball and volleyball courts, competition pools and year-round programmes.The project will give another Oklahoma community access to a similar range of sporting facilities.The NBA's October 2026 announcement stated that the Trae Young Family Foundation had donated more than $4 million towards the development and advancement of recreational and athletic facilities in Oklahoma.This figure refers to the foundation's wider work in the state. It should not be confused with the $4 million contribution towards the Norman center or treated as the total cost of that facility.The Yukon announcement also came as Young began a new chapter with the Washington Wizards. Despite moving to a different city for his NBA career, he continued supporting projects in the state where he grew up.Trae Young committed $100,000 to two Washington organisationsFollowing his arrival in Washington, Young and his family foundation committed $100,000 to two local organisations. DC College Access Program (DC CAP) and DC Central Kitchen each received $50,000.DC CAP works with students attending Washington, D.C., public and public charter high schools. Its programmes help students enrol in college and complete their education.DC Central Kitchen focuses on food access and employment training. It provides school meals and hunger relief programmes while also offering culinary job training.The two organisations work in different areas, but both support people facing challenges in their communities.The NBA and the National Basketball Players Association announced Young as the offseason winner of the Bob Lanier Community Assist Award on October 19, 2026. The award recognised his work in Washington and Oklahoma, including his support for education, food access and youth recreation.The NBA and NBPA Foundation also announced a separate collective donation of $20,000 to DC CAP and DC Central Kitchen. This amount was in addition to the $100,000 commitment made by Young and his foundation.Speaking about the recognition, Young said, "Being recognized for this award means so much to me, because the work I do off the court matters just as much as the work I do on the court."He also spoke about his connection to both communities."My goal is to keep showing up for both communities, to create opportunities for them, and to remind them that somebody is in their corner," Young said. Young visited hospital patients and worked with more than 175 childrenYoung also took part in several community events around his birthday in Washington.He visited students at Thurgood Marshall High School, Friendship Technology Prep and Monument Academy. During these visits, he spoke about mental health, perseverance and dealing with difficult situations.He also made a surprise visit to pediatric patients at MedStar Georgetown Hospital. Young spent time with the children and their families and gave patients signed jerseys.The three-day programme included a free Pro-Am Day at Oxon Hill High School and the From the Point Youth Skills Clinic at Prince George's County Community College.More than 175 children attended the four-hour clinic. Young joined the drills and worked directly with participants alongside coaches from the Jr. Wizards youth basketball programme.These activities formed part of the community work recognised by the NBA.The Bob Lanier Community Assist Award is named after the late NBA Hall of Famer, who served as an NBA League Office executive and NBA Cares ambassador for more than 30 years. The award recognises players who contribute to their communities during the NBA season and offseason.Young has now received the honour three times. His community work has covered several areas, from helping fund a sports facility in Norman to supporting college access and hunger relief in Washington. The planned Yukon center will also extend his foundation's work in Oklahoma.The two-year period between the Norman facility's opening and his latest Washington commitment shows how his community projects have continued alongside his NBA career.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: No 3 Utah remains undefeated with thrilling win over No 9 BYU behind Heisman finalist Devon Dampier's epic day
articles.summary: Utah defeated BYU 28-20 in the Holy War as quarterback Devon Dampier was fantastic in the win, firmly planting himself in the Heisman conversation.
articles.body: The Holy War may have kicked off early, but both Utah and BYU were up to the task and delivered an instant classic. No. 3 Utah (9-0) defeated No. 9 BYU 28-20 on Saturday at Rice-Eccles Stadium in a thrilling game that had major College Football Playoff and Big 12 championship implications. Utes quarterback Devon Dampier was outstanding in the win and vaulted himself into the Heisman Trophy conversation. Dampier was 14 of 26 for 177 yards and two touchdowns while rushing for 87 yards and two touchdowns. For Utah, the win was its 15th straight, the longest active winning streak in college football, and also snapped a three-game losing streak to BYU. The Utes remain undefeated and are in the driver's seat to make the Big 12 championship game and are all but assured to make the College Football Playoff. articles.title: Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg buys house for his mother, who saved his basketball career
articles.summary: Yaxel Lendeborg's path to the NBA doesn't happen without his mother's support, according to the man himself.
articles.body:
According to Yaxel Lendeborg, there is no college stardom or NBA contract without his mother Yissel Raposo. He just paid her back accordingly.

The Golden State Warriors rookie accomplished a "lifelong goal" recently by surprising his mother with a new house , documenting the reveal in a YouTube video titled, "This one's for Mama Yax." Raposo is overcome with emotion upon being told, "Welcome home," fighting tears as she walks to the doorway.

Lendeborg reveals in the video that securing the home took two to three months.

"There is no gesture big enough to properly say thank you for all the love, sacrifice, and support my mom has poured into me but this moment was pretty special and one I'll never forget. She deserves it all. For me, it's bigger than basketball. It's about making sure the people who believed in me get to enjoy the blessings too."

The 24-year-old isn't overstating the impact his mother, who was diagnosed with Stage 4 appendix cancer last year, had on him.

As Lendeborg recalled in an article for The Players' Tribune in February, titled "How My Mom Saved My Life" , there was a time he was struggling through high school to the point where he wasn't just academically ineligible for the basketball team, but at risk of failing to graduate.

He says Raposo pushed him to complete a heavy workload of courses at a local community college, which allowed him to play basketball in his senior year. She then quietly arranged to get him a spot in a showcase for Dominican players, leading to an offer from Arizona Western College, which she made him take despite his significant reservations.

What followed was a wild success story in the transfer-heavy world of modern college basketball. Lendeborg starred at Arizona Western, transferred to UAB and excelled there, then joined Michigan for a single season. He was the leading scorer for a historically good Wolverines team, winning an NCAA title, All-American honors and the Big Ten Player of the Year award.

Despite being one of the older players in his draft class, the Warriors selected Lendeborg 12th overall. His mom was there, of course, and they shared an emotional moment once his name was called.

Lendeborg's NBA career is already off to a strong start. His 21.0 points and 7.1 rebounds per game are both second in his draft class, while his 4.1 assists per game rank fourth. He is among the favorites for the NBA Rookie of the Year award.

After an 0-3 start, the Warriors have won six straight games.

articles.title: Nuggets hold off Pacers in NBA Mexico City game
articles.summary: Denver star Nikola Jokic scored 19 points and grabbed 13 rebounds as the Nuggets held off Indiana's second-half surge to triumph 114-102 on Saturday in the N...
articles.body:
Denver star Nikola Jokic scored 19 points and grabbed 13 rebounds as the Nuggets held off Indiana's second-half surge to triumph 114-102 on Saturday in the NBA's Mexico City game.

Three-time NBA Most Valuable Player Jokic added eight assists, coming up just shy of a triple-double.

Cameron Johnson added 18 points and Jamal Murray chipped in 16 for the Nuggets, who saw a 27-point lead sliced to seven midway through the fourth quarter but held on for the victory before a sellout crowd of more than 20,000 at Mexico City's Arena CDMX.

Indiana's Pascal Siakam led all scorers with 23 points.

The league headed south of the border for its 16th regular-season contest in Mexico.

Along with 19 pre-season games, the country has hosted the most NBA games outside of the United States and Canada.

The Pacers, again playing without injured Tyrese Haliburton, jumped to a quick 5-0 lead and were up 7-4 when the Nuggets produced a 10-0 scoring run to seize a lead they wouldn't relinquish.

Denver pushed the advantage to as many as 27 on the way to a 64-41 halftime edge.

The Pacers hit back with a 37-point third quarter and pulled within 102-95 on a Jarace Walker running basket with 7:27 remaining.

The Nuggets responded with a quick basket from Spencer Jones and a thunderous Aaron Gordon dunk as they kept the Pacers at bay.

The game was one of seven on Saturday's slate, which also featured the Cleveland Cavaliers hosting the defending champion New York Knicks.

It's the second heavyweight clash in as many nights in Cleveland, where the Cavs beat LeBron James and the Eastern Conference-leading Philadelphia 76ers on Friday.

It's a rematch of last season's Eastern Conference finals, in which the Knicks swept the Cavs on the way to their first NBA title since 1973.

articles.title: Jalen Brunson, KAT Lead Knicks Over Cavs, Box Score Stats, Highlights for Harden, Spida, Top Players
articles.summary: Jalen Brunson lifted the New York Knicks past James Harden and the Cleveland Cavaliers 109-97 on the road Saturday after a strong third quarter.
articles.body:
Jalen Brunson lifted the New York Knicks past James Harden and the Cleveland Cavaliers 109-97 on the road Saturday after a strong third quarter.

The defending champion Knicks entered Saturday's matchup as 4.5-point favorites over the Cavaliers, according to FanDuel Sportsbook , sealing the deal after taking an 18 point lead into the fourth quarter.

The Knicks improved to 5-4 after a rough start to the season, shaking off the championship blues after opening the year with three consecutive losses.

Cleveland fell to 5-5 as Harden struggled Saturday and Donovan Mitchell led the Cavaliers with 37 points.

Brunson finished with 31 points, six rebounds and nine assists to help lift the Knicks to an impressive win. His strong night followed a hot first half in which he tallied 20 points, four rebounds and four assists to lead the team to a 10-point lead at the half.

Towns added 29 points after an explosive second half, along with three rebounds and two steals after scoring 18 points and six rebounds by halftime.

OG Anunoby finished with 15 points, Mikal Bridges and Landry Shamet both added nine.

Harden was held to five points, two rebounds and three assists at the half. Finishing with just seven points, two rebounds, five assists. Mitchell led the team at the half with 11 points, finishing with 37 points, two steals and one block.

Peyton Watson and Evan Mobley each added 12 points in the loss.

The Knicks will host the Milwaukee Bucks on Tuesday, while the Cavaliers will hit the road to face the Charlotte Hornets on Monday.

articles.title: Steph Curry Breaks LeBron James Record as Warriors Beat Magic, Box Score Stats, Highlights, Reaction
articles.summary: Stephen Curry made NBA history as the Golden State Warriors defeated the Orlando Magic by the final score of 126-119 in overtime on Saturday night.
articles.body:
Stephen Curry made NBA history as the Golden State Warriors defeated the Orlando Magic by the final score of 126-119 in overtime on Saturday night.

Curry recorded his 16th game with at least 40 points since turning 35 years old, surpassing LeBron James for the most 40-point performances among players older than 35.

Curry finished with 41 points, six rebounds and six assists in 36 minutes on the floor against Orlando. He shot 13-of-19 from the field and 5-of-10 from behind the arc while hitting all 10 of his free throw attempts.

The Warriors started off strong on Saturday, leading 31-19 at the end of the first quarter before extending their advantage to 57-41 at halftime.

Orlando looked much sharper on both ends of the court in the third quarter, outscoring Golden State 37-20 in the period.

The two teams battled down the stretch of the fourth quarter until Magic forward Jamal Cain tapped in an offensive rebound to tie the score at 110 before the end of regulation.

Orlando took a 118-117 lead in overtime, but Golden State ended the game on a 9-1 run to emerge victorious. Curry's late heroics were crucial in the victory, scoring 19 of his 41 points in the fourth quarter and overtime.

The Warriors improved to 7-3, winning their seventh straight game after beginning their season with an 0-3 record.

Curry has already established himself as one of the greatest players in NBA history, but the 12-time All-Star hasn't shown too many signs of slowing down at 38 years old.

He's averaging 31.3 points per game this season, ranking No. 3 among all players.

Curry is also recording 4.6 assists, 4.0 rebounds and 1.1 steals on a nightly basis while compiling 49.7/44.7/98.5 shooting splits.

The Warriors will face the New Orleans Pelicans in their next game, with tip-off on Monday at 10 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Kenny Atkinson Clarifies Viral 'Analytically' Comment, Admits Knicks 'Dominated' Cavs in ECF Sweep
articles.summary: The New York Knicks defeated the Cleveland Cavaliers 109-97 on Saturday in their first matchup since New York swept the Cavs in four games in last season's Eastern Conference Finals.
articles.body:
The New York Knicks defeated the Cleveland Cavaliers 109-97 on Saturday in their first matchup since New York swept the Cavs in four games in last season's Eastern Conference Finals.

Following Game 3 of that matchup, Cavs head coach Kenny Atkinson told reporters that "analytically," the team had won two-of-three games per the expected score metric.

Those remarks went viral en route to the Cavs eventually losing Game 4, 130-93.

On Saturday, Atkinson provided more context to his comments when asked about them.

"I think when you look back on it and take the context of the question, I'm not sure that was taken into account, which I know was a little bit of a lesson for me — like, you can just take a sound bite (and run with it)," Atkinson said (h/t Joe Vardon of The Athletic).

"I would just say there was no coach more complimentary of the Knicks and honest about our performance and how they dominated us," Atkinson said. "So you live and learn a little bit with those things. But like I said, 99 percent of my comments were how they dominated us. They were by far the better team. I answered the question, as it was taken, (which was) 'And you're down 3-0, what hope do you have of even giving to your guys?'

"We get a lot of information … and I wasn't lying in that sense, but in no sense was it like, 'Oh, man, we deserve to be winning.' Like zero — zero — thought of that."

Atkinson's points here make sense, and he was ultimately trying to find some positivity in the face of a nearly impossible task for his team to come back down 3-0 in the series, which hasn't been done in NBA history.

Ultimately, the Knicks were a buzzsaw in the 2026 playoffs, going 16-3 overall and winning 14 of their final 15 games (including 13 straight). Cleveland stood in its way and lost its four games in the series by a combined 77 points.

The Cavs were competitive in Game 1. They were up 22 points in the fourth quarter but suffered a devastating collapse before falling 115-104 in overtime.

Cleveland couldn't hit a shot in Game 2 (38.8 percent from the field, 25.7 percent from three) and lost 109-93. New York's starting lineup dominated Game 3 (98 points) in a 121-108 win, and the Knicks outscored the Cavs by seven points at minimum in each quarter en route to the closing 37-point Game 4 win (130-93).

Jalen Brunson (31 points) and Karl-Anthony Towns (29 points, 13 rebounds) were the heroes Saturday for New York, which moved to 5-4. Cleveland fell to 5-5.

articles.title: Aday Mara hace su mejor partido en la NBA y le llueven elogios y motes: 'El inspector Gadget', 'Big Spain'...
articles.standfirst: El pívot, de nuevo titular, luce en la paliza de los Thunder con 18 puntos (8/10 en tiros), nueve rebotes y tres tapones
articles.summary: El pívot, de nuevo titular, luce en la paliza de los Thunder con 18 puntos (8/10 en tiros), nueve rebotes y tres tapones
articles.body: Aunque apenas se note por los resultados (8-2), las lesiones de Jalen Williams, Cason Wallace y Chet Holmgren, tres de sus puntales, fueron un duro golpe para los Thunder. Pero los de Oklahoma están demostrando tener una enorme profundidad de banquillo para paliar las consecuencias. Y ahí aparece la espigada figura de Aday Mara, que sigue creciendo como la espuma en sus primeros pasos en la NBA. En la paliza a los Wizards, que sufrieron a una defensa tremenda (114-75), firmó su mejor actuación. El pívot español anotó 18 puntos (8/10 en tiros incluido un triple), ocho rebotes, tres asistencias y tres tapones. Sigue sin faltar a su cita con los 'gorros' en cada encuentro y se mantiene en el quinto puesto de la estadística. Mientras él jugó, los Thunder ganaron por 17. Exprimiendo cada minuto que pasa en pista. Mara fue titular por segunda vez compartiendo juego interior con Isaiah Hartenstein y ocupando el lugar del lesionado Holmgren, que alucina con el novato español: "Es como El inspector Gadget. Sus brazos son como eternos". Kenrich Williams prefiere llamarle "Big Spain". Tras los intentos de ponerle un mote, las alabanzas. "Está evolucionando ante nuestros ojos. Va a ser un jugador especial en la NBA", dice. El entrenador Mark Daigneault también tuvo palabras para un Mara que tiene impacto en cuanto salta a la pista: "Ha hecho un gran trabajo. Ha sido realmente consistente. Ha jugado minutos impactantes todas y cada una de las noches, lo cual es difícil de hacer para un jugador novato, especialmente en esa posición, que es difícil". Por talla, intimidación, recursos cerca del aro, capacidad de pase y conocimiento del juego, Mara empieza a ser ya un referente de los Thunder. Todo ello lo destaca Williams: "Es superhabilidoso, tiene un instinto realmente bueno para jugar, puede pasar el balón, tiene un toque especial alrededor del aro y ¡mide 2,21 metros!". Jared McCain asegura que "cuando combina todas esas condiciones, no hay muchas personas que puedan detenerlo". El mejor en las filas de Oklahoma volvió a ser Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, que se fue a los 30 puntos en solo tres cuartos. Con amplias diferencias en el marcador (máxima de 43) y en el segundo partido en noches consecutivas, era innecesario seguir en pista. Jared McCain le secundó con 19 puntos en un equipo que desde las lesiones de sus titulares ha ganado cinco de sus siete encuentros y acumula cuatro triunfos seguidos. Enfrente unos Wizards sin Anthony Davis que estuvieron negados en el tiro ante la aguerrida defensa de Oklahoma. Hicieron 29/98 en tiros de campo con 7/43 en triples. El novato AJ Dybantsa, número 1 del draft, fue su mejor efectivo con 19 puntos y Alex Sarr logró un doble-doble con 15+14.

articles.standfirst: El alero de los Warriors, uno de los mejores rookies de la temporada, grabó el emotivo momento en el que hace entrega de las llaves
articles.summary: El alero de los Warriors, uno de los mejores rookies de la temporada, grabó el emotivo momento en el que hace entrega de las llaves
articles.body: El primer sueldo en la carrera profesional de Yaxel Lendeborg encontró un emotivo destino: se lo gastó en comprar una casa a su madre. El novato de los Warriors grabó un vídeo en el que se ve el momento en el que le da la sorpresa y le entrega las llaves. "Bienvenida a casa”, dice el alero de 24 años y 2,06 metros ante su emocionada madre, Yissel Raposo. "No hay gesto suficiente para agradecer todo el amor, el sacrificio y el apoyo que mi madre me ha brindado, pero este momento fue muy especial y uno que jamás olvidaré. Ella se lo merece todo. Para mí, esto va más allá del baloncesto. Se trata de asegurarme de que quienes creyeron en mí también disfruten de las bendiciones", asegura Lendeborg. El rookie fue compañero de Aday Mara en la Universidad de Míchigan y rechazó un salario de 9 millones de dólares en la NCAA por sus derechos NIL (siglas en inglés de name, image y likeness, esto es: nombre, imagen y semejanza). Decidió presentarse al draft y salió elegido en el undécimo lugar, un puesto antes que el pívot español. Según las tablas salariales, ganará 6,0 millones de dólares en su primera temporada en la NBA. Con su primer cheque le ha hecho un gran regalo a su madre. Lendeborg creció muy unido a ella. El jugador contó en un artículo publicado en 'The Players Tribune' en febrero que fue su madre quien salvó su carrera cuando estuvo a punto de abandonar el baloncesto durante su último año de instituto debido al duelo por la muerte de su abuelo. Ahora, Lendeborg es una de las nuevas sensaciones de la NBA y un serio aspirante al galardón de Rookie del Año. Está promediando 21,0 puntos, 7,1 rebotes y 4,1 asistencias. Además, ha demostrado desde el primer día mucha personalidad y gran competitividad. En su estreno en la competición tuvo un pique y un acalorado cruce de palabras con Luka Doncic, al que puso en apuros con su defensa. Y eso, viendo el nivel del esloveno, ya es mucho decir.

articles.body: Un día más en la oficina para Victor Wembanyama, que hizo 29 puntos en sólo 24 minutos para que los Spurs vencieran cómodamente en Portland (103-125) y sumaran su octava victoria consecutiva. Los de San Antonio perdieron sus dos primeros partidos de la temporada y ante sus aficionados, pero cuando su estrella ha ido cogiendo sensaciones se han colocado segundos del Oeste y tienen la mejor activa de la NBA. Wembanyama igualó su menor cantidad de minutos y de tiros de campo en lo que va de campaña. Lanzó sólo 13 veces, como en el horrible estreno ante los Thunder (1/13). Sin necesidad de que Wemby mostrara su versión más alienígena, los minutos y los puntos estuvieron repartidos entre los Spurs, que aún no han perdido fuera de casa tras ganar sus cuatro encuentros. Nadie estuvo más de media hora en pista, Devin Vassell hizo 15 puntos, Stephon Castle y el suplente Julian Champagnie llegaron a 14 y Dylan Harper, 13.

articles.title: Austin Reaves predicted Luka Doncic’s 40-point scoring tear over a year before Lakers star delivered
articles.summary: Austin Reaves appears to have known exactly what Luka Doncic was capable of, with a prediction he made more than a year ago resurfacing as the Lakers star en...
articles.body:
Austin Reaves appears to have known exactly what Luka Doncic was capable of, with a prediction he made more than a year ago resurfacing as the Lakers star enjoys a remarkable start to the 2026-27 NBA season.

Doncic is averaging 40.1 points through his first 10 games, helping Los Angeles move to an 8-2 record and the top of the Western Conference.

The six-time All-Star has been particularly impressive over his last four outings, scoring 45, 42, 40 and 53 points as the Lakers recorded four consecutive wins.

Austin Reaves predicted Luka Doncic could average 40 points for Los Angeles Lakers

ESPN reporter Dave McMenamin recently brought attention to an old article featuring Reaves' prediction that Doncic could average 40 points per game while still helping the Lakers win.

At the time, Doncic had already shown what he could produce offensively, recording 91 points across two games to average 45.5, although Los Angeles split those contests.

Reaves' prediction now looks remarkably accurate, with Doncic leading the league in scoring while the Lakers continue to win.

His efficiency has also been impressive. Doncic is shooting 49.8 per cent from the field and 41.9 per cent from three-point range, both career-high figures.

The Slovenian is contributing beyond scoring, too, averaging 7.8 rebounds, 7.7 assists and 1.7 steals per game.

His dominance is reflected across several other statistical categories. Doncic leads the NBA in field goals made and attempted, three-pointers made and attempted, as well as free throws made and attempted.

He is currently making 12.2 field goals from 24.6 attempts per game, alongside 5.8 three-pointers from 13.8 attempts and 9.9 free throws from 11.3 attempts.

However, the Lakers could face a concern ahead of their next outing against the Detroit Pistons. Doncic was listed as questionable on the front end of a back-to-back, potentially leaving Los Angeles without its leading scorer as it looks to extend its four-game winning streak.

articles.standfirst: El base brilla en su estreno con los Coachella Valley Lakers: 22 puntos, cinco rebotes y siete asistencias
articles.summary: El base brilla en su estreno con los Coachella Valley Lakers: 22 puntos, cinco rebotes y siete asistencias
articles.body: Ante su falta de minutos en la NBA, Bronny James fue enviado esta semana a los Coachella Valley Lakers, el equipo vinculado de la franquicia angelina en la G League y no ha tardado en destacar. En el estreno de la competición hizo 22 puntos, cinco rebotes, siete asistencias y una recuperación en la victoria sobre los Salt Lake City Stars por 104-98. El hijo de LeBron salió de inicio y dejó buenas sensaciones. "Simplemente juego a mi manera. De la misma forma en que lo hacía con los Lakers cuando quedaban dos minutos o lo que fuera y salía a la pista. Sólo intento jugar con inteligencia y ser agresivo", dijo Bronny tras su buena actuación. Esta temporada apenas había protagonismo con los Lakers y cuando lo tuvo fue para mal, como cuando los Raptors casi remontan un partido con un parcial de 0-11 en un minuto cuando él salió junto a otros reservas. En lo que iba de temporada, Bronny había aparecido en cinco partidos estando en pista un total de 12:23 minutos. En ese tiempo, sus cifras habían sido muy pobres: cuatro puntos y ningún rebote ni asistencia. Con él en pista, los angelinos habían perdido por 27. Bronny ya había pasado por la G League en sus dos anteriores temporadas en la NBA y había demostrado que es una competición que se adapta mejor a su nivel y sus condiciones. En los 25 encuentros que ha disputado ahí, el base había promediado 18,4 puntos con un 49,6% de acierto en tiros de campo, 4,4 asistencias y 4,0 rebotes. "Me encanta jugar al baloncesto y poder venir aquí y rendir es bueno para mí y para mi ánimo. Siempre que me llamen, estoy dispuesto a venir a jugar", aseguró. Su necesidad de minutos es evidente si quiere seguir desarrollando su juego. De ahí que fuera enviado a la G League. "El mensaje fue muy simple. Simplemente, necesitas entrenar y necesitas jugar”, le dijo el entrenador JJ Redick cuando el envió al conjunto vinculado. En una temporada tan larga, quizás pueda regresar en algún momento al equipo NBA, pero de momento tratará de crecer ahí.

articles.title: Landing Spots for NBA's Best Free Agents Right Now
articles.summary: NBA free agency isn't just a summertime and training-camp affair.
articles.body:
NBA free agency isn't just a summertime and training-camp affair.

Midseason signings usually have the same impact as July acquisitions, but they can help teams plug holes created by injuries or unaddressed shortcomings. They are especially useful for buying time until the NBA's unofficial trading window opens up on Dec. 15.

Available free agents will be included based on their ability to have a short- and/or longer-term impact. Proposed destinations will factor in team needs, cap sheets, roster-spot logistics and competitive timelines.

2025-26 Stats: 8.0 PTS, 4.0 REB, 4.4 AST, 0.8 STL

Vince Williams Jr. is recovering from a torn ACL in his left knee and is bound to miss a huge chunk of the 2026-27 campaign. A smart team will consider getting in on the ground floor of his return rather than competing for his services this winter or next offseason.

The Chicago Bulls have the gradual timeline that allows for this type of flier. Their defense is also a disaster from the outside in. Blowing up opposing offenses just so happens to be Williams' calling card.

Fretting over how V-Dub looks post-ACL injury shouldn't be a factor. His value is rooted in guarding up. That's more about strength than explosion.

Touch-and-go three-point shooting is the bigger concern. Williams' 36.8 percent clip he posted last year in limited action on catch-and-fire triples was the second-highest of his career. While that's potential cause to scare off playoff teams, it shouldn't be a deterrent for the Bulls.

2025-26 Stats: 6.7 PTS, 5.8 REB, 1.8 AST, 0.4 STL

Injuries to Jusuf Nurkić (foot) and Jaren Jackson Jr. (knee) have depleted the Utah Jazz's big-man ranks. Truth be told, reuniting with Kevin Love won't help them get by.

Sure, he can still hit a three and grab a defensive rebound. But he's not doing their shaky defense any favors.

Let's all agree that they shouldn't care.

Injuries and all, the Jazz are underachieving at the offensive end. This increasingly feels like a team that needs an adult in the room. Love checks that bellwether box.

Utah would have to create a roster spot to make this happen. That shouldn't be a deal-breaker. Tony Bradley is buried behind Mo Bamba and Jaxson Hayes in the pecking order and won't see the light of day once Nurkić gets back.

And who knows, given how little the Jazz have used Kyle Filipowski following his return from offseason back surgery, perhaps Love can scrounge up some floor-spacing-big minutes here and there.

2025-26 Stats: 6.7 PTS, 2.3 REB, 0.8 AST, 0.4 STL

Ochai Agbaji has now been rejected twice during the 2026-27 calendar season alone. He failed to make the New York Knicks' final roster and then the Oklahoma City Thunder reneged on an agreement with him after finding out Chet Holmgren would be missing at least eight to 10 weeks with a right knee injury.

Call me a sucker, but I'm still riding for a 6'5" combo wing who has routinely proved his defensive mettle. The Indiana Pacers should, too.

Injuries have ripped through their roster. You can watch the entire Marvel catalog in the time it takes to pore over one of their pregame reports. And while a reserve center and ball-handler have emerged as sore spots, they've always needed a flier on another wing defender.

According to BBall Index, Agbaji has ranked no lower than the 87th percentile in matchup difficulty since entering the league. He has also spent more than two-thirds of his career possessions guarding primary ball-handlers.

Three-point shooting remains the swing skill. Agbaji is a career 33.9 percent marksman from beyond the arc. But he shot 35.5 percent as a rookie and 39.9 percent in 2024-25. Spotting up inside Indiana's offense should help him recapture that touch—particularly when Tyrese Haliburton returns.

Bookkeeping is all that stands in the way of this match. The Pacers have an open roster spot and enough room beneath the first apron to add Agbaji. But Indy hasn't paid the tax in over 20 years. Unless it plans to start now, the front office may be hesitant to sign anyone before offloading salary.

Runner-Up Destination: Golden State Warriors

2025-26 Stats: 17.4 PTS, 5.2 REB, 7.4 AST, 2.2 STL

Even though the Milwaukee Bucks are teeming with guards, waiving Kevin Porter Jr.'s $5.4 million salary from this season's ledger is a red flag. That he remains unsigned following their decision is even more alarming.

KPJ's offensive pedigree remains tantalizing. He has excellent size, is a better from-scratch passer than advertised and can generate half-court rim pressure. His three-point clip has dipped over the last two seasons, but he's still rated inside the 79th percentile or higher of catch-and-shoot efficiency from deep through three of the past four years, according to BBall Index .

Although the Miami Heat's defense is giving them more trouble than their offense, they're exhausting the usage of Giannis Antetokounmpo, Pelle Larsson and Donovan Mitchell. Another ball-handler and scorer would go a long way.

The need for one is especially urgent so long as Tim Hardaway Jr. and Andrew Wiggins are struggling to torch twine. And KPJ would also be a nice audible to Klay Thompson minutes on nights in which defenses are relentlessly targeting the latter.

2025-26 Stats: 7.9 PTS, 3.9 REB, 2.1 AST, 1.0 STL

Bruce Brown failing to land a gig with the New York Knicks doesn't prove that he's washed. They needed a center more than another guard. The Oklahoma City Thunder are a different story.

Losing Jalen Williams (leg) and Cason Wallace (shoulder) potentially for the season leaves the once-upon-time title favorites light on defensive versatility and offensive optionality. They've already signed Dalen Terry, who has some intrigue at both ends. But they're not in a position to rule out other wing options unless they plan to make a bigger trade.

Despite standing 6'4", Brown fits within OKC's players-who-guard-up motif. Naz Reid, Kevin Durant and Cooper Flagg ranked among his 10 highest-volume defensive assignments last season. That says more about the state of the 2025-26 Denver Nuggets, but it's also more than a footnote.

What Brown lacks in bankable shooting he makes up for with connective skills. He keeps the ball moving; knows how to cut and relocate in the half-court; keeps defenses guessing from short-roll territory; can get out in transition; and has the capacity to run the occasional pick-and-roll.

OKC would have to create a roster spot to sign Brown and doesn't have any clear-cut candidates. Nikola Topić comes closest after the Thunder declined his team option. That said, they're not beholden to keeping Terry, either.

Dan Favale is a National NBA Writer for Bleacher Report. Follow him on Bluesky ( @danfavale ), and subscribe to the Hardwood Knocks podcast, co-hosted by Bleacher Report's Grant Hughes .

articles.title: El Barça resiste a un gran Río Breogán y a las lesiones
articles.standfirst: Brizuela y Parra (16 puntos cada uno) comandan la séptima victoria seguida de los azulgranas, que vieron retirarse a Punter y Evbuomwan
articles.summary: Brizuela y Parra (16 puntos cada uno) comandan la séptima victoria seguida de los azulgranas, que vieron retirarse a Punter y Evbuomwan
articles.body: El Barcelona mantiene su línea ascendente. Sumó su séptima victoria consecutiva, tercera en la Liga Endesa, tras derrotar con mucho trabajo a un Río Breogán que demostró por qué es una de las sensaciones de la competición. Como acostumbran, los azulgranas resistieron los envites de su rival y se sobrepusieron a los problemas físicos de Kevin Punter y Tosan Evbuomwan, que tuvieron que dejar el encuentro. Los culés estuvieron mucho tiempo por detrás en el marcador, acumularon 24 pérdidas que hicieron estéril su dominio del rebote y dieron el golpe definitivo en el último periodo, cuando impidieron anotar a los gallegos en seis ataques seguidos y abrieron una importante brecha con protagonismo de Joel Parra. Acabaría con 16 puntos. El alero, que pasa por uno de los mejores momentos de su carrera, anotó cinco puntos del tirón, incluido un triple muy complicado, para poner el 91-83, que era la máxima renta culé. Los esfuerzos visitantes en el último tramo, comandados por Danko Brankovic (15), fueron insuficientes. La puntería del Barça desde el tiro libre y un sólido Tyrese Martin (10+10) aseguraría un triunfo rematado por un mate sobre la bocina del propio Parra. Darío Brizuela, que tuvo un feliz cumpleaños, también alcanzó los 16 puntos. Lleva una serie de partidos siendo decisivo más ejerciendo de base ante las bajas de Umoja Gibson y Juan Núñez. Él tiró de los culés en un buen inicio (17-10) y después soltando picotazos. El Breogán tenía problemas para defender su aro, pero mejoró mucho en el segundo cuarto. Tanto que maniató al Barça y un parcial de 2-13 al ritmo de Dominik Mavra (12 y cinco asistencias) le puso ocho arriba (29-37). Brankovic empezaba a castigar por dentro y Tevin Brown (15) por fuera. El trabajo de Olivier Nkamhoua alivió a los locales, que alcanzaron el descanso a rebufo de su rival (39-40). En la reanudación, otro tirón gallego aprovechando el despertar de Francis Alonso. Llegaba como el máximo anotador de la Liga Endesa con 21,1 puntos de media, pero al intermedio no se había estrenado. Acabó con ocho, pero 0/5 en triples. El Breogán se fue por siete (43-50) y el Barça encontró un salvavidas en Olek Balcerowski, que terminaría con 14 puntos Tremendos minutos del pívot sacando varios 2+1, incluido uno con un mate descomunal, y corriendo a la contra (55-52). Ahí comenzó un intercambio de golpes que mantuvo la igualdad hasta el tramo final. Amida Brimah alternaba errores y aciertos para los visitantes, Justin Robinson aparecía como siempre que el Barça anda apurado, Josh Nebo se comió el aro varias veces, también Andersson García... Así hasta el 89-91, cuando el Breogán acumuló errores ante unos azulgranas más aplicados en defensa y que resolvieron otro triunfo en el tramo final. Atentos a la evolución de los tocados. El viernes, visita al Panathinaikos. 99 - Barça (23+16+30+30): Robinson (13), Martin (10), Ubal (-), Parra (16), Balcerowski (14), -cinco inicial-, Punter (6), Umude (1), Brizuela (16), Nkamhoua (11), Evbuomwan (4), Minaya (4), Nebo (4). 91 - Río Breogán (20+20+30+21): Bolton (11), Peris (-), Brown (15), Andric (7), Brankovic (15), -cinco inicial-, Alfonso (8), García (4), Brimah (5), Aranitovic (9), Mavra (12), Quintela (-), Kasibabu (5). Árbitros: Rafael Serrano, Jorge Martínez y Ariadna Chueca. Señalaron falta técnica a Aleksander Sekulic (min.27) por parte del Barça. Eliminaron a Justin Robinson por parte del Barça. Incidencias: Partido correspondiente a la séptima jornada de la Liga Endesa disputado en el Palau Blaugrana (Barcelona) ante 3.875 espectadores.

articles.title: High school athlete cursed out by Seattle Storm owner runs against trans athlete at state championship
articles.summary: Ahnaleigh Wilson ran through a bone stress injury at the Pasco, WA state cross country finals, lining up against the Camas transgender athlete.
articles.body: It was a cross-country course filled with twists, turns, hills and switchbacks. There was nothing round about it. But for Eastmont High junior Ahnaleigh Wilson, this was a case of things coming full circle. More than two years ago, Wilson finished second to a trans athlete in a Junior Olympic track race. That set her on a path of speaking out against biological boys competing in girls' sports. If her name looks familiar, it's because she's the one Seattle Storm co-owner Celeste Keaton cursed out at a WNBA game in July for holding a sign reading, "Thank You Sophie (Cunningham) For Speaking Up For Girls!" It brought a high school girl to tears, but as you'll learn, it takes a lot more than that to stop Ahnaleigh. SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM FAN WHO WAS CONFRONTED BY STORM CO-OWNER OPENS UP ON INCIDENT AND FACING TRANS ATHLETES Since Keaton's tirade, quite a bit has happened in the world of Washington state transgender athletes. For the last month and a half, a male runner from Camas High who switched to the girls team midseason has dominated the headlines. After opening the season 76th in a boys' JV race, he crossed over to win a varsity girls' meet and knock female runners out of regional and state qualifying spots. Well, guess who was lined up against him in Saturday's 4A girls state finals at Sun Willows Golf Course? That's right — one Ahnaleigh Wilson. Wilson racing was no guarantee. Not just because she'd considered taking a stand against having to compete against a boy, but because she had a bone stress injury in her right fibula she feared might develop into a fracture. Her parents encouraged her not for health reasons. She didn't listen. "I worked really hard this season, and I mean, I like running. So I wanted to run. I wanted to try at least," Wilson said. It might have been good social-media material for activists had Wilson walked off in protest, but that wasn't going to happen. Plus, she'd already done enough in that department — regularly speaking in defense of girls and women despite her relatively shy nature. She'd survived all the emotional abuse her detractors had thrown her way. Saturday was about surviving the physical. BIOLOGICAL MALE COMPETING IN GIRLS' CROSS-COUNTRY RACE DENIES ANOTHER RUNNER AND HER TEAM A TRIP TO STATE A healthy Wilson likely would have finished somewhere in the top third of Saturday's 155-girl field. Her usual time of 19:30 would have been good for 49th place. But this was not a healthy Wilson. This was a high school junior slogging through a 5000-meter course with searing pain every other step. Ahnaleigh said she thought about quitting multiple times mid-race. But the cheers from the crowd kept her going. And we aren't talking about the ones from her parents, friends or coaches. We're talking about random supporters who knew her name because of everything she'd fought for. "There were a few times I didn't know if I was going to finish, and I heard people I didn't recognize their voices, but there were people cheering for me, and that was really cool," she said. Wilson's final time? 22:58.30 — which placed her 150th. The Camas male, meanwhile, finished 23rd, which wasn't fast enough to put him on the podium reserved for the top 16 runners. This was his first race since Tuesday's election, when Washington voters decisively passed Initiative 638, which will enforce the separation of biological boys and girls in K-12 sports once it takes effect. And even though many runners at Saturday's race were relieved the measure got through, they were still motivated to outrun the boy in the girls race. One was Skyview High runner Charlie Garrett, who, alongside teammate Sierra Retzlaff, walked off the start line in protest of the Camas runner last month. She'd heard that the boy told his teammates that his goal was to beat them every time since that act, and while he was successful in doing so Saturday (Garrett and Retzlaff finished 39th and 92nd, respectively), Garrett took solace in the fact that she wouldn't have to face him again. WASHINGTON HS GIRLS BLAST MALE ATHLETE PARTICIPATING IN TRACK MEET: 'DON'T THINK THAT THAT'S RIGHT OR FAIR' "I guess the motivation (to beat him) is just that I don't want my spot to be taken away by someone who shouldn't be in my race. That's my main motivation" said Garrett, a junior. "I didn't do it this season — and I won't have to this season. But I mean, me and my mom are very competitive people, so I think it just runs in the blood to try and do better than the person who's causing us stress." Echoing that sentiment was Kamiakin High sophomore Lauren Baumann. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! "My goal was to beat the guy from Camas because I don't think he should be racing in a girls race," said Baumann, who finished 11 spots behind him. "When he passed me at the 800 and I tried to stay with him but couldn't, it made me feel really really mad and just that I couldn't do anything to stop it. But I'm glad that he won't be able to run next year." I-638 could go into effect as soon as December 3, although there may be legal challenges delaying its implementation. But girls such as Wilson, Garrett and Retzlaff — all of whom played critical roles in getting it passed — are taking their metaphorical victory laps. That said, perhaps nobody was as emotional Saturday as Ahnaleigh's mom, Elizabeth, who broke down in tears after her daughter's race. "I can't believe she went out and did that with a bone stress...that's just heart," Elizabeth said. "She started this journey racing a boy, and she ended it, and hopefully this will be the last time a boy competes against girls." OUTKICK IS NOW AVAILABLE ON THE FOX NEWS APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD X-rays will reveal whether Ahnaleigh — who was limping after the race — has a stress fracture. But she proved something Saturday. Whether it's a state cross country race or a ballot initiative — no matter how painful, she is going to finish what she started.

articles.title: Doc Rivers' Controversial Diss on Giannis Addressed by Heat HC Erik Spoelstra
articles.summary: Miami Heat coach Erik Spoelstra wasn't worried about critical comments from former Milwaukee Bucks head coach Doc Rivers when it came to figuring out the best way to maximize Giannis Antetokounmpo.
articles.body:
Miami Heat coach Erik Spoelstra wasn't worried about critical comments from former Milwaukee Bucks head coach Doc Rivers when it came to figuring out the best way to maximize Giannis Antetokounmpo.

"Look, I like Doc, and I respect him," Spoelstra said Saturday, per Eric Nehm of The Athletic. "This is our business now."

Rivers appeared on Thursday's episode of The Bill Simmons Podcast and said coaching Antetokounmpo was "difficult" and "not easy" at times (h/t Nehm). He also said it was "hard to get right" when attempting to balance the overall team success and Antetokounmpo's style of play.

Miami brought in the future Hall of Famer this offseason in one of the NBA's marquee moves of the past year, but it has been a rocky start. It is just 3-6 overall, although it has shown signs of improvement following an 0-4 start.

Spoelstra said the team is "making some progress" as it attempts to "develop a defense that's meeting our potential."

He also said offensively "we went into the season thinking that that would be a process, playing with somebody that commands so much attention. That's a different style than some of the guys that have come here, that have played before. We'll be able to figure that all out. We've already made a lot of strides."

For his part, Rivers coached Antetokounmpo in Milwaukee during the previous 2.5 seasons and went 97-103. Injuries played a major role in the failure to live up to expectations, as Antetokounmpo was sidelined for a first-round loss to the Indiana Pacers in 2024 before Damian Lillard was out for some of the first-round loss to the same team the next year.

Coaching Antetokounmpo is surely an adjustment, as he is someone who plays with the ball in his hands, aggressively attacks the rim and isn't a great three-point shooter.

But he is also an all-time great who led the Bucks to the 2021 title as the NBA Finals MVP.

Spoelstra is in the process of figuring things out with his team's new star and didn't want to directly address Rivers' comments.

articles.title: Bronny James' Lakers Status Updated After Breakout Game in G League Win
articles.summary: Bronny James impressed in the G-League, and now he is returning to the Los Angeles Lakers.
articles.body:
Bronny James impressed in the G-League, and now he is returning to the Los Angeles Lakers.

Ayomide Adeduyite of Athlon Sports noted the Lakers recalled James and Cameron Carr ahead of their four-game road trip that starts Sunday against the Detroit Pistons and features games against the Atlanta Hawks, Milwaukee Bucks and Phoenix Suns.

Los Angeles previously sent them to the Coachella Valley Lakers, and James thrived during the G-League's team against the Salt Lake City Stars with 22 points, seven assists and five rebounds in a 104-98 win.

He also said, "It's good to be in a new environment."

James, who is the son of the legendary LeBron James, was buried in the Lakers' rotation in the early portion of the season. While it was just a brief appearance at the G-League, it was also an opportunity for the 22-year-old to get some playing time instead of just sitting on the end of the team's bench.

"The messaging was very simple," Lakers head coach JJ Redick said, per Benjamin Royer of the Orange County Register . "It's just: you guys need reps and you guys need to play."

James is averaging just 2.4 minutes per game in his five appearances for the Lakers this season.

Los Angeles also hasn't needed him much, as it is off to an excellent 8-2 start with Luka Dončić leading the way as an early MVP candidate. Dončić is averaging a stunning 40.1 points per game on the campaign and dropped 53 in Friday's win over the Portland Trail Blazers.

It was his fourth straight game with at least 40 points and second game of the season with more than 50.

There is no doubt the Lakers are Dončić's team at this point, but James will look to carve out a role in the rotation following his appearance in the G-League.

articles.title: Dillon Brooks Appears to Troll Kevin Durant, Addresses 'S--t-Talking' Rockets Players in Suns' Win
articles.summary: Phoenix Suns wing Dillon Brooks seemingly took a subtle shot at Kevin Durant following his team's 102-99 win over the Houston Rockets.
articles.body:
Phoenix Suns wing Dillon Brooks seemingly took a subtle shot at Kevin Durant following his team's 102-99 win over the Houston Rockets.

Brooks cited the Suns' "culture" when asked about their defensive performance. They held Durant to 5-of-14 shooting.

"We play hard, we play together and we try to challenge ourselves to do great," Brooks said . "So shout out to Mat."

One could read his remark as a reference to the back-and-forth Durant had with Suns team governor Mat Ishbia on social media last month:

Brooks has built his reputation on being an irritant on and off the floor, and he doesn't think twice about challenging notable stars. Following Saturday's game, he said in the locker room he was "s--t-talking to other guys" on Houston and will "just say what I need to say."

Brooks' approach has been successful for him individually, and his teams have occasionally fed off his intensity on the floor. He has carved out a long career and signed a $73 million extension with Phoenix.

It's safe to assume the 30-year-old doesn't have a ton of friends around the league, though. Earlier this week, Golden State Warriors star Draymond Green sounded off on the veteran forward after they had a tense moment in a game.

Brooks probably sees that as evidence that his strategy is still working.
